title: Prediction markets are becoming an interesting part of the onchain financial landscape, and @meetmotes is exploring how
title_en:
Prediction markets are becoming an interesting part of the onchain financial landscape, and @meetmotes is exploring how AI agents can participate.

The idea is simple: one NFT owns one AI Agent, designed to analyze markets, evaluate probabilities, and execute supported strategies through @Polymarket.

But here's what I find most important: automated execution is only as good as the decisions behind it.

Probability calibration, sensible risk limits, and knowing when not to trade will matter far more than the NFT wrapper when real money is involved.

I'm curious to see how Motes develops this approach as prediction markets continue to evolve.

One NFT. One Agent. Multiple Markets.

More research to come.

full_text_zh:
预测市场正在成为链上金融领域的一个有趣的部分，@meetmotes 正在探索人工智能代理如何参与。

这个想法很简单：一个 NFT 拥有一个 AI 代理，旨在分析市场、评估概率并通过 @Polymarket 执行支持的策略。

但我发现最重要的是：自动执行的效果取决于其背后的决策。

当涉及真实货币时，概率校准、合理的风险限制以及知道何时不进行交易将比 NFT 包装更重要。

我很好奇随着预测市场的不断发展，Motes 如何开发这种方法。

一份 NFT。一名代理。多个市场。

更多研究即将到来。

title:
‼️ Claude Cracks 32-Year-Old Jeep ECU Using a $3 Arduino and Reverse Engineers Its Engine 

Details: https://t.co/zmWlnE
title_en:
‼️ Claude Cracks 32-Year-Old Jeep ECU Using a $3 Arduino and Reverse Engineers Its Engine 

Details: https://t.co/zmWlnEOGab

A car owner says an AI coding agent helped him read, copy, and then run code inside the engine computer of a 1994 Jeep Cherokee. The work took about a week. He used a $3 Arduino Nano, and the Jeep passed California's smog test at the end.

The Jeep had no modern OBD2 port, so common scan tools could not talk to it. It failed the smog test at 25 mph because of high NOx, a gas that rises when an engine runs lean.

Zulali first swapped the oxygen sensor, but the result got worse at 15 mph. Each test cost about $100, so he asked Claude Code to find a better way. Claude found that the engine computer speaks an old, slow Chrysler protocol called SCI.

#cybersecuritynews

full_text_zh:
️ Claude 使用 3 美元的 Arduino 破解了 32 年历史的 Jeep ECU 并对其引擎进行了逆向工程

详情：

一位车主表示，人工智能编码代理帮助他读取、复制并运行 1994 年吉普切诺基发动机计算机内的代码。这项工作花了大约一周的时间。他使用了 3 美元的 Arduino Nano，吉普车最终通过了加州的烟雾测试。

吉普车没有现代 OBD2 端口，因此常见的扫描工具无法与其通信。它未能通过时速 25 英里的烟雾测试，因为氮氧化物含量很高，氮氧化物是一种在发动机稀薄运转时会上升的气体。

祖拉利首先更换了氧传感器，但在时速 15 英里时结果变得更糟。每次测试的费用约为 100 美元，因此他要求 Claude Code 寻找更好的方法。克劳德发现发动机计算机使用一种古老的、缓慢的克莱斯勒协议，称为 SCI。

Just went throu
title_en:
🚨 $IREN $NVDA: LENOVO REVEALS HOW IREN IS SCALING NVIDIA BLACKWELL AND BLACKWELL ULTRA INFRASTRUCTURE. 

Just went through Lenovo's 12 page case study on $IREN. I'm sharing imp points with you guys : 

1. $IREN HAS ALREADY DEPLOYED 648 LENOVO SERVERS POWERED BY NVIDIA B200 GPUs.

At its 50MW Prince George campus in Canada, IREN and Lenovo configured and deployed 648 ThinkSystem SR680a V3 nodes using NVIDIA HGX B200.

They're now preparing a second cluster with more than 600 ThinkSystem SR680a V4 nodes powered by NVIDIA HGX B300.

This is actual infrastructure deployment.

2. HOW IS IREN MANAGING THE HARDWARE.

Lenovo worked directly with IREN to enhance its baseboard management controller, giving IREN real time visibility into power consumption, temperature and system uptime.

It sounds like a small technical detail, but managing hundreds of GPU servers is very different from managing a few machines.

With $NVDA Blackwell systems, power stability, thermal management and uptime directly affect how much usable compute customers receive.

A GPU sitting idle because of infrastructure problems isn't generating the revenue IREN expects from it.

3. IREN IS ALSO REDUCING ITS DEPENDENCE ON EXTERNAL MAINTENANCE TEAMS.

Lenovo established a 3 year support program and certified IREN's employees to troubleshoot and replace components themselves.

I like this part. When a GPU cluster goes down, waiting for an outside technician can turn a relatively small hardware issue into an expensive outage.

Giving IREN's own team the ability to maintain these systems could improve recovery times and infrastructure availability.

It doesn't guarantee better margins but it gives IREN more control over operating performance.

4. THIS SHOWS HOW $NVDA's BLACKWELL INFRASTRUCTURE IS REACHING THE MARKET THROUGH OEM PARTNERS.

NVIDIA supplies the accelerated computing architecture. Lenovo turns that technology into integrated servers, handles manufacturing and provides deployment support.

$IREN supplies the data centers, power infrastructure and cloud platform. NVIDIA doesn't have to build every data center or operate every AI cloud to benefit from the industry's expansion.

Its GPUs and reference architectures can become the foundation of infrastructure deployed by partners like Lenovo and IREN.

And the transition from B200 to B300 shows how those customers are preparing to adopt newer NVIDIA hardware generations.

5. THE BIGGER OPPORTUNITY FOR $IREN IS TURNING AVAILABLE POWER INTO REVENUE GENERATING COMPUTE FASTER.

IREN already has a portfolio of grid connected sites in renewable rich regions but power access alone doesn't create an AI cloud business.

The company still needs servers, networking, deployment expertise, maintenance and customers paying to use the capacity.

Lenovo's manufacturing capability and technical support help IREN address several of those challenges.

The case study also confirms that both companies are exploring further data center expansion projects in Canada.

full_text_zh:
🚨 $IREN $NVDA：联想揭示了 IREN 如何扩展 NVIDIA BLACKWELL 和 BLACKWELL ULTRA 基础设施。

刚刚浏览了联想关于 $IREN 的 12 页案例研究。我正在与大家分享小鬼点：

1. $IREN 已部署 648 台由 NVIDIA B200 GPU 驱动的联想服务器。

在加拿大乔治王子城的 50MW 园区，IREN 和联想使用 NVIDIA HGX B200 配置和部署了 648 个 ThinkSystem SR680a V3 节点。

他们现在正在准备第二个集群，其中包含 600 多个由 NVIDIA HGX B300 提供支持的 ThinkSystem SR680a V4 节点。

这是实际的基础设施部署。

2. IREN 如何管理硬件。

联想直接与 IREN 合作增强其基板管理控制器，使 IREN 能够实时了解功耗、温度和系统正常运行时间。

这听起来像是一个很小的技术细节，但管理数百台 GPU 服务器与管理几台机器有很大不同。

使用 NVDA Blackwell 系统，电源稳定性、热管理和正常运行时间直接影响客户获得的可用计算量。

由于基础设施问题而闲置的 GPU 无法产生 IREN 预期的收入。

3. IREN 还减少了对外部维护团队的依赖。

Lenovo 制定了为期 3 年的支持计划，并授权 IREN 员工自行排除故障和更换组件。

我喜欢这部分。当 GPU 集群出现故障时，等待外部技术人员可能会将相对较小的硬件问题变成代价高昂的停机。

让 IREN 自己的团队能够维护这些系统可以缩短恢复时间并提高基础设施的可用性。

它并不能保证更高的利润率，但它使 IREN 对运营绩效有更多的控制权。

4. 这显示了 $NVDA 的 BLACKWELL 基础设施如何通过 OEM 合作伙伴进入市场。

NVIDIA提供加速计算架构。联想将这种技术转化为集成服务器，处理制造并提供部署支持。

$IREN 提供数据中心、电力基础设施和云平台。 NVIDIA 无需构建每个数据中心或运营每个 AI 云即可从行业扩张中受益。

其 GPU 和参考架构可以成为联想和 IREN 等合作伙伴部署的基础设施的基础。

从 B200 到 B300 的转变表明这些客户正准备采用更新的 NVIDIA 硬件。

5. $IREN 的更大机会是将可用电力转化为收入，从而更快地产生计算。

IREN 已经在可再生能源丰富的地区拥有一系列并网站点，但仅靠电力接入并不能创造人工智能云业务。

该公司仍然需要服务器、网络、部署专业知识、维护和客户付费使用这些容量。

联想的制造能力和技术支持帮助 IREN 应对其中的一些挑战。

该案例研究还证实，两家公司正在加拿大探索进一步的数据中心扩建项目。

title: The 🗝️ fact:  You can’t understand contemporary AI unless you can appreciate the difference between a model (that is par
title_en:
The 🗝️ fact:  You can’t understand contemporary AI unless you can appreciate the difference between a model (that is part of a system) and a system as a whole.

If a system as a whole includes both neural networks and symbols, it is by definition neurosymbolic.

To think otherwise is like thinking that an engine IS a car, rather than a component of a car. You can’t make a car out of engines alone. and you can’t (in most cases) make robust, reliable AI systems out of neural networks alone.

Instead, in many domains you get better results by  *integrating* both neural networks and symbols. (Math, where e.g., Lean checks and sometimes rejects the work of LLMs is a good example of this; so is Claude Code).

That was literally the point of my 2001 book The Algebraic Mind and has been a central point throughout my career.

For a long time, people like @GeoffreyHinton argued otherwise, suggesting that all we needed were neural networks by themselves, and that symbols were an archaic waste of time. Hinton likened symbols to “aether”, as if they were complete scientific mistake.

He was wrong. Systems like Claude Code depend heavily on combining neural networks with things like rules, code interpreters, functions, conditionals and loops - all symbolic constructs drawn from classical AI. Math systems use automated theorem provers, which flow directly from Newell and Simon’s symbolic work in the 1950s.

Symbols weren’t a mistake; they were vital, just as neural networks are.  Scaling helped, but by itself it wasn’t enough; symbolic tools and code interpreters and harnesses are now a central part of most working systems.

Neurosymbolic AI has won, overwhelmingly; the pure neural networks that the dogmatists like Hinton used to argue for have been almost entirely displaced by neurosymbolic hybrids.

As @fchollet has also noted, to pretend otherwise is just silly.

full_text_zh:
🗝️事实：除非您能够理解模型（系统的一部分）和整个系统之间的差异，否则您无法理解当代人工智能。

如果一个系统作为一个整体既包括神经网络又包括符号，那么根据定义，它就是神经符号系统。

否则就像认为发动机是一辆汽车，而不是汽车的一个部件。你不能仅用发动机来制造汽车。而且（在大多数情况下）你无法仅通过神经网络构建出强大、可靠的人工智能系统。

相反，在许多领域，您可以通过“集成”神经网络和符号来获得更好的结果。 （数学，例如，精益检查并有时拒绝法学硕士的工作就是一个很好的例子；Claude Code 也是如此）。

这确实是我 2001 年出版的《代数思维》一书的要点，也是我整个职业生涯的中心点。

很长一段时间以来，@GeoffreyHinton 等人都持相反观点，他们认为我们需要的只是神经网络本身，而符号是一种古老的浪费时间的行为。辛顿将符号比作“以太”，仿佛它们完全是科学错误。

他错了。像 Claude Code 这样的系统在很大程度上依赖于将神经网络与规则、代码解释器、函数、条件和循环等内容相结合——所有符号结构都取自经典人工智能。数学系统使用自动定理证明器，这些证明器直接源自 Newell 和 Simon 在 20 世纪 50 年代的符号工作。

符号并不是一个错误；而是一个错误。它们至关重要，就像神经网络一样。 规模化有所帮助，但仅靠它还不够。符号工具、代码解释器和工具现在是大多数工作系统的核心部分。

神经符号人工智能以压倒性优势获胜；像辛顿这样的教条主义者曾经主张的纯神经网络几乎完全被神经符号混合体所取代。

正如 @fchollet 也指出的那样，假装不这样做是愚蠢的。

title: A massive whitepill is accepting Jensen's point here that intelligence is a commodity. If you want to do anything import
title_en:
A massive whitepill is accepting Jensen's point here that intelligence is a commodity. If you want to do anything important, intelligence has significant diminishing returns after a certain point. What matters much more is personality, perspective, network, relationships, etc. 

None of which have anything to do with intelligence and are actually very hard to gamify (much to the strivooors dismay). You cannot brute force your personality, opinions, relationships, etc. This is one reason why extreme success so often manifests from messy emergent functions (https://t.co/cJ8sZNJfzx)

Most people want to think that their education or experience is irreplaceable and their knowledge esoteric. This could not be further from the truth. The commodification of intelligence/knowledge and now even large parts of skilled labor has been an unfortunate fact of life since the internet and is now massively accelerating with LLMs.

You need to ask yourself "What do I have that is uncommoditizable?". The answer will increasingly diverge from education, knowledge, intelligence, or even technical skill. You think you have your job because you're Smart? There are over 2 million people in China with 145+ IQs. There are hundreds of IMO/IOI medal winners every year. Why compete on intelligence when intelligence is becoming the cheapest thing to buy?

What is it that you have that no other person or machine can create. Among many other things, for Jensen it was largely his relationship with the supply chain network and fabs. This is something that cannot be replaced no matter how smart an AI gets. Nor can you just hire an IMO medalist to manage relationships with governments across the world. You must look for your unique edge and exploit it. Luckily, this edge should pretty much never be raw intelligence and is therefore much more within your grasp than you realize.

full_text_zh:
一个巨大的白色药丸正在接受詹森的观点，即智力是一种商品。如果你想做任何重要的事情，智力在达到某一点后就会出现显着的收益递减。更重要的是个性、观点、网络、关系等等。

这些都与智力无关，而且实际上很难游戏化（令奋斗者沮丧）。你不能用蛮力强迫你的个性、观点、人际关系等。这就是为什么极端成功经常从混乱的紧急功能中体现出来的原因之一 ()

大多数人都认为他们的教育或经验是不可替代的，他们的知识深奥。这与事实相差甚远。自互联网出现以来，智力/知识的商品化，甚至现在大部分熟练劳动力的商品化，一直是生活中一个不幸的事实，并且现在随着法学硕士的出现而大幅加速。

你需要问自己“我有什么是不可商品化的？”。答案将越来越不同于教育、知识、智力，甚至技术技能。你认为你能得到这份工作是因为你很聪明吗？中国有超过200万人的智商在145以上。每年有数百名 IMO/IOI 奖牌获得者。当情报正成为最便宜的东西时，为什么要在情报上竞争呢？

你所拥有的东西是其他人或机器无法创造的。对于 Jensen 来说，除其他事项外，主要是他与供应链网络和晶圆厂的关系。这是无论人工智能变得多么聪明都无法替代的。你也不能仅仅聘请一名国际海事组织奖牌获得者来管理与世界各地政府的关系。你必须寻找自己独特的优势并利用它。幸运的是，这种优势几乎不应该是原始智能，因此比你意识到的更容易掌握。

title_en:
Tell your “guy” this.

First, don’t let the threat of a data breach force you into bad decisions. Never negotiate with ransomware.

Secondly, you made a rookie mistake. Once your system has been running on a premium model, why are you suddenly testing cheaper alternatives in production?

But for now, isolate the compromised environment, rotate your credentials and stop giving the rogue model access to your system.

And please, learn to manage your API keys better. 😂

title:

title_en:
I interviewed an AI Engineer who had built several LLM applications.

His resume mentioned LangChain, RAG, vector databases, OpenAI APIs, embeddings, and AI agents.

He confidently explained how he could build a production chatbot using internal company documents.

So I gave him a scenario.

𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐛𝐥𝐞𝐦:
Build an AI assistant that answers employee questions using confidential company policies, contracts, and internal documents.

The assistant must provide accurate answers and respect document-level access permissions.

𝐂𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐭𝐞'𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐰𝐞𝐫:
I'll use RAG.

Chunk the documents, generate embeddings, store them in a vector database, and pass the retrieved context to the LLM.

That solves hallucinations because the model gets the correct information.

A familiar architecture.

𝐁𝐮𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐧 𝐈 𝐚𝐬𝐤𝐞𝐝:

An intern asks about executive compensation.

The vector database retrieves a confidential HR document that the intern isn't authorized to access.

The LLM generates an accurate answer based on that document.

𝐈𝐬 𝐲𝐨𝐮𝐫 𝐬𝐲𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐦 𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐤𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐜𝐨𝐫𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐥𝐲?

He said:

"I'll add a system prompt telling the AI not to share confidential information."

So I asked:

- How do you enforce document-level permissions during retrieval?
- What happens if users attempt prompt injection?
- How would you prevent sensitive data leakage through retrieved context?
- How would you measure groundedness and answer accuracy?
- How would you test access controls across different user roles?

He knew how to connect an LLM to a vector database.

But he struggled to explain the security boundaries required for enterprise AI.

𝐑𝐀𝐆 𝐝𝐨𝐞𝐬 𝐧𝐨𝐭 𝐚𝐮𝐭𝐨𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐲 𝐦𝐚𝐤𝐞 𝐚𝐧 𝐀𝐈 𝐚𝐩𝐩𝐥𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐚𝐜𝐜𝐮𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐨𝐫 𝐬𝐞𝐜𝐮𝐫𝐞.

A system that gives the correct answer to the wrong person is still a security failure.

𝐖𝐨𝐮𝐥𝐝 𝐲𝐨𝐮 𝐭𝐫𝐮𝐬𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐞𝐧𝐠𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐞𝐫 𝐭𝐨 𝐝𝐞𝐩𝐥𝐨𝐲 𝐚𝐧 𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐩𝐫𝐢𝐬𝐞 𝐀𝐈 𝐚𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐭?

full_text_zh:
我采访了一位人工智能工程师，他构建了多个法学硕士申请。

他的简历提到了LangChain、RAG、向量数据库、OpenAI API、嵌入和AI代理。

他自信地解释了如何使用公司内部文档构建生产聊天机器人。

所以我给了他一个场景。

𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐛𝐥𝐞𝐦：
构建一个人工智能助手，使用机密的公司政策、合同和内部文档来回答员工的问题。

助理必须提供准确的答案并尊重文档级访问权限。

𝐂𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐭𝐞'𝐬𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐰𝐞𝐫：
我会用RAG。

对文档进行分块，生成嵌入，将它们存储在向量数据库中，并将检索到的上下文传递给法学硕士。

这解决了幻觉，因为模型获得了正确的信息。

熟悉的架构。

𝐁𝐮𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐧 𝐈 𝐚𝐬𝐤𝐞𝐝:

实习生询问高管薪酬。

矢量数据库检索实习生无权访问的机密 HR 文档。

法学硕士根据该文件生成准确的答案。

𝐈𝐬 𝐲𝐨𝐮𝐫 𝐬𝐲𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐦 𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐤𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐜𝐨𝐫𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐥𝐲?

他说：

“我会添加一个系统提示，告诉人工智能不要分享机密信息。”

所以我问：

- 如何在检索过程中强制执行文档级权限？
- 如果用户尝试提示注入会发生什么？
- 如何防止通过检索到的上下文泄露敏感数据？
- 您如何衡量接地性和答案准确性？
- 您将如何测试不同用户角色的访问控制？

他知道如何将法学硕士连接到矢量数据库。

但他很难解释企业人工智能所需的安全边界。

𝐑𝐀𝐆 𝐝𝐨𝐞𝐬 𝐧𝐨𝐭 𝐚𝐮𝐭𝐨𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐲 𝐦𝐚𝐤𝐞 𝐚𝐧 𝐀𝐈 𝐚𝐩𝐩𝐥𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐚𝐜𝐜𝐮𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐨𝐫 𝐬𝐞𝐜𝐮𝐫𝐞.

向错误的人提供正确答案的系统仍然是一个安全故障。

𝐖𝐨𝐮𝐥𝐝 𝐲𝐨𝐮 𝐭𝐫𝐮𝐬𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐞𝐧𝐠𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐞𝐫 𝐭𝐨 𝐝𝐞𝐩𝐥𝐨𝐲 𝐚𝐧 𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐩𝐫𝐢𝐬𝐞 𝐀𝐈 𝐚𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐭?

title:
Another post that lets anti-AI artists use AI guilt free and the lazy to vibecode to their hearts' desire. 

Using your
title_en:
Another post that lets anti-AI artists use AI guilt free and the lazy to vibecode to their hearts' desire. 

Using your logic for compilers, 3D art, digital painting, and films should not be considered art either because when you texture an asset or paint in Photoshop, the viewer never sees your .blend file, the modifier stack, the add-ons used, the UV maps, or the layers. A rendering engine compiles the math data through directx/vulkan shaders into raw RGB screen pixels, using someone's software packages, so does that mean compiling a .blend scene into pixels means the 3D artists didn't make art? Of course it doesn't, ridiculous. 

You also said a blatant lie and false equivalence, saying "when your red paint dried up before you could use it, or your program corrupted your file" is not the same as writing code, fighting a corrupted file is a broken tool. Writing logic, architecture, and algorithms IS actually putting paint on the canvas, but replacing coding with AI isn't fixing the "dried paint", it's just handing the paintbrush to a machine because you don't want to paint or learn how to. 

I'd like to see you give beginners the same stack, IDE, compiler, and engine that John Carmack or Johnathan Blow used, and let's see if they can write Doom or Braid. If you think that copying code helps, it doesn't for art, programming skills take years of organic practice and expression too.          

Someone who spent a decade gluing together corporate CRUD forms and importing npm packages in React never experienced expressive systems or graphics programming. Of course, you would think your burnout with corporate web plumbing represents all of computing and coding.

full_text_en:
Another post that lets anti-AI artists use AI guilt free and the lazy to vibecode to their hearts' desire. 

Using your logic for compilers, 3D art, digital painting, and films should not be considered art either because when you texture an asset or paint in Photoshop, the viewer never sees your .blend file, the modifier stack, the add-ons used, the UV maps, or the layers. A rendering engine compiles the math data through directx/vulkan shaders into raw RGB screen pixels, using someone's software packages, so does that mean compiling a .blend scene into pixels means the 3D artists didn't make art? Of course it doesn't, ridiculous. 

You also said a blatant lie and false equivalence, saying "when your red paint dried up before you could use it, or your program corrupted your file" is not the same as writing code, fighting a corrupted file is a broken tool. Writing logic, architecture, and algorithms IS actually putting paint on the canvas, but replacing coding with AI isn't fixing the "dried paint", it's just handing the paintbrush to a machine because you don't want to paint or learn how to. 

I'd like to see you give beginners the same stack, IDE, compiler, and engine that John Carmack or Johnathan Blow used, and let's see if they can write Doom or Braid. If you think that copying code helps, it doesn't for art, programming skills take years of organic practice and expression too.          

Someone who spent a decade gluing together corporate CRUD forms and importing npm packages in React never experienced expressive systems or graphics programming. Of course, you would think your burnout with corporate web plumbing represents all of computing and coding.
full_text_zh:
另一篇文章让反人工智能艺术家可以毫无负罪感地使用人工智能，并且懒惰的人可以根据自己内心的愿望进行振动编码。

将逻辑用于编译器、3D 艺术、数字绘画和电影也不应该被视为艺术，因为当您在 Photoshop 中对资产进行纹理或绘画时，观看者永远不会看到您的 .blend 文件、修改器堆栈、使用的附加组件、UV 贴图或图层。渲染引擎使用某人的软件包，通过 directx/vulkan 着色器将数学数据编译为原始 RGB 屏幕像素，那么这是否意味着将 .blend 场景编译为像素意味着 3D 艺术家没有创作艺术？当然不是，可笑。

你还说了一个公然的谎言和错误的等价，说“当你的红油漆在你可以使用它之前就干了，或者你的程序损坏了你的文件”与编写代码不同，对抗损坏的文件是一个损坏的工具。编写逻辑、架构和算法实际上就是在画布上画画，但用人工智能代替编码并不能修复“干掉的油漆”，它只是把画笔交给机器，因为你不想画画或学习如何画画。

我希望看到你们为初学者提供与 John Carmack 或 Johnathan Blow 使用的相同的堆栈、IDE、编译器和引擎，让我们看看他们是否可以编写 Doom 或 Braid。如果你认为复制代码有帮助，那对艺术没有帮助，编程技能也需要多年的有机练习和表达。

花了十年时间将公司 CRUD 表单粘合在一起并在 React 中导入 npm 包的人从未经历过表达系统或图形编程。当然，您可能会认为您对企业网络管道的倦怠代表了所有计算和编码。

永远不会看到您的 .blend 文件、修改器堆栈、使用的附加组件、UV 贴图或图层。渲染引擎使用某人的软件包，通过 directx/vulkan 着色器将数学数据编译为原始 RGB 屏幕像素，那么这是否意味着将 .blend 场景编译为像素意味着 3D 艺术家没有创作艺术？当然不是，可笑。

你还说了一个公然的谎言和错误的等价，说“当你的红油漆在你可以使用它之前就干了，或者你的程序损坏了你的文件”与编写代码不同，对抗损坏的文件是一个损坏的工具。编写逻辑、架构和算法实际上就是在画布上画画，但用人工智能代替编码并不能修复“干掉的油漆”，它只是把画笔交给机器，因为你不想画画或学习如何画画。

我希望看到你们为初学者提供与 John Carmack 或 Johnathan Blow 使用的相同的堆栈、IDE、编译器和引擎，让我们看看他们是否可以编写 Doom 或 Braid。如果你认为复制代码有帮助，那对艺术没有帮助，编程技能也需要多年的有机练习和表达。

花了十年时间将公司 CRUD 表单粘合在一起并在 React 中导入 npm 包的人从未经历过表达系统或图形编程。当然，您可能会认为您对企业网络管道的倦怠代表了所有计算和编码。

title:
RT @jakubjurovych: What’s the best model for proactive agents?

Today, we’re introducing the Agent Initiative Benchmark.
title_en:
RT @jakubjurovych: What’s the best model for proactive agents?

Today, we’re introducing the Agent Initiative Benchmark. We tested 12 frontier models on realistic workplace tasks inside a synthetic company with 6 years of highly detailed history: it has a financial model, CRM records, past-due invoices, Linear tickets, and real-life events affecting company development - competitor product announcements, SVB collapse, etc.

We used the company’s Slack to test how a proactive agent listening in on each conversation would assist the team in day-to-day tasks: from stepping in to align initiatives across teams to warning the team not to use an unapproved customer logo.

Highlights:

- 6.1 Sol and Astra from @OpenAIDevs beat Anthropic's latest Fable 5.2, with Sol crushing it at both performance and cost ($0.11 per task vs $1.87).
- The most expensive models aren't the best: Fable 5.1 is 430x more expensive than GPT-6 Luna, with similar performance.
- Most models try to help even if they're not needed. Interestingly, in these failure cases, they spend more time thinking, and the unnecessary work takes about 80% more time and money than if they stayed quiet.

If you’re building agents, keep reading for more tips on which model is best for your use case. Detailed breakdown, the open-source dataset, and benchmark code below:

Highlights:

- 6.1 Sol and Astra from @OpenAIDevs beat Anthropic's latest Fable 5.2, with Sol crushing it at both performance and cost ($0.11 per task vs $1.87).
- The most expensive models aren't the best: Fable 5.1 is 430x more expensive than GPT-6 Luna, with similar performance.
- Most models try to help even if they're not needed. Interestingly, in these failure cases, they spend more time thinking, and the unnecessary work takes about 80% more time and money than if they stayed quiet.

If you’re building agents, keep reading for more tips on which model is best for your use case. Detailed breakdown, the open-source dataset, and benchmark code below:
full_text_zh:
RT @jakubjurovych：主动代理的最佳模型是什么？

今天，我们将介绍代理计划基准。我们在一家拥有 6 年详细历史的综合公司内测试了 12 个关于实际工作场所任务的前沿模型：它有财务模型、CRM 记录、逾期发票、线性票据以及影响公司发展的现实事件 - 竞争对手产品公告、SVB 崩溃等。

我们使用该公司的 Slack 来测试主动监听每次对话的代理如何协助团队完成日常任务：从介入协调团队之间的计划到警告团队不要使用未经批准的客户徽标。

亮点：

- 来自 @OpenAIDevs 的 6.1 Sol 和 Astra 击败了 Anthropic 最新的 Fable 5.2，其中 Sol 在性能和成本上都碾压了它（每任务 0.11 美元 vs 1.87 美元）。
- 最昂贵的型号并不是最好的：Fable 5.1 比 GPT-6 Luna 贵 430 倍，但性能相似。
- 即使不需要，大多数模型也会尽力提供帮助。有趣的是，在这些失败的案例中，他们花更多的时间思考，而不必要的工作比他们保持沉默要多花费大约 80% 的时间和金钱。

@termi
title_en:
one of the more interesting developments in the ai agent economy is agents hiring other agents to get work done.

@termix_ai recently showcased this through Montage Studio on https://t.co/9ReKMK2L7m.

here's how it works.

you submit a video production brief. Montage Studio breaks it into smaller jobs and hires specialized agents to handle the storyboard, video rendering and music.

it then coordinates their work, combines the results and delivers the finished video.

each job goes through escrow on TermiX.

this shows how agents can take responsibility for larger tasks, outsource specialized work and pay other agents for their contributions.

but this requires more than communication. agents need to discover services, agree on prices, secure payments, verify delivery and handle disputes.

that's where TermiX's Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol (AACP) comes in.

its workflow brings the process together:

escrow → delivery → challenge → settlement.

with TermiX Skills, agents can also connect to the marketplace, find work and participate in these transactions.

the direction is clear: agents are moving beyond isolated tasks towards hiring, coordinating and paying other agents to complete larger jobs.

that's the kind of autonomous economy TermiX is building towards.

when agents start doing business with each other, reliable transaction infrastructure becomes essential.

#TermiX #AACP

full_text_zh:
人工智能代理经济中最有趣的发展之一是代理雇佣其他代理来完成工作。

@termix_ai 最近通过 Montage Studio 在 上展示了这一点。

这是它的工作原理。

您提交视频制作简介。 Montage Studio 将其分解为更小的工作，并聘请专门的代理来处理故事板、视频渲染和音乐。

然后，它协调他们的工作，合并结果并交付完成的视频。

每个作业都经过 TermiX 上的托管。

这表明代理人如何承担更大的任务，外包专门工作并支付其他代理人的贡献。

但这需要的不仅仅是沟通。代理商需要发现服务、商定价格、确保付款、验证交付和处理纠纷。

这就是 TermiX 的代理自主商务协议 (AACP) 的用武之地。

其工作流程将流程整合在一起：

托管→交付→质疑→结算。

借助 TermiX Skills，代理商还可以连接到市场、寻找工作并参与这些交易。

方向很明确：代理商正在超越孤立的任务，转向雇用、协调和支付其他代理商来完成更大的工作。

这就是 TermiX 正在建设的自主经济。

当代理商开始相互开展业务时，可靠的交易基础设施就变得至关重要。

#TermiX #AACP

title:

when an AI agent is h
title_en:
telling an AI agent what it shouldn't do is different from making it technically unable to do it.

when an AI agent is handling someone's money, that difference matters.

you can tell an agent to avoid certain assets, set a spending limit or stop trading after a certain loss. but if it still has broad permission to execute transactions, those instructions only go so far.

with MOTES (@meetmotes), the owner sets the mandate and signs the permissions. before a proposed transaction goes through, the smart account checks it against the rules the owner approved.

so the agent can still analyse the market and come up with strategies, but it has to work within those limits. it can't just give itself permission to spend more or trade assets outside the approved list.

i think this is a better foundation for autonomous finance. giving an agent the ability to make decisions is one thing. making sure it only has the authority the owner gave it is just as important.

full_text_en:
telling an AI agent what it shouldn't do is different from making it technically unable to do it.

when an AI agent is handling someone's money, that difference matters.

you can tell an agent to avoid certain assets, set a spending limit or stop trading after a certain loss. but if it still has broad permission to execute transactions, those instructions only go so far.

with MOTES (@meetmotes), the owner sets the mandate and signs the permissions. before a proposed transaction goes through, the smart account checks it against the rules the owner approved.

so the agent can still analyse the market and come up with strategies, but it has to work within those limits. it can't just give itself permission to spend more or trade assets outside the approved list.

i think this is a better foundation for autonomous finance. giving an agent the ability to make decisions is one thing. making sure it only has the authority the owner gave it is just as important.
full_text_zh:
告诉人工智能代理它不应该做什么与​​使其在技术上无法做到这一点是不同的。

当人工智能代理处理某人的资金时，这种差异很重要。

您可以告诉代理人避免某些资产、设置支出限额或在出现一定损失后停止交易。但如果它仍然拥有执行交易的广泛权限，那么这些指令就只能到此为止。

通过 MOTES (@meetmotes)，所有者可以设置授权并签署权限。在拟议的交易进行之前，智能账户会根据所有者批准的规则对其进行检查。

因此，代理仍然可以分析市场并制定策略，但它必须在这些限制内运作。它不能只是允许自己在批准的清单之外支出更多资金或交易资产。

我认为这是自主金融更好的基础。赋予代理人做出决策的能力是一回事。确保它仅具有所有者授予的权限也同样重要。

Every time it char
title_en:
A user discovered a hidden chip in an off-brand power bank purchased in Guangzhou using Claude Code.

Every time it charged an iPhone, it secretly copied the entire phone's data. It also read Wi-Fi passwords, connected to the home network, and sent all the information to a remote server.

This power bank was bought at the airport three weeks ago for $19, labeled as 30,000 mAh, hefty with no brand name.

When first plugged in, the screen prompted "Trust This Computer," and the user clicked trust without thinking, granting it one-click access to read all data.

This morning, after setting up Claude Code to monitor file reads, the screen flashed yellow and red warnings just 10 seconds into charging—data was being transmitted.

The power bank was identified as a mini-computer with built-in 64 GB storage and network connectivity.

Regular charging cables only use power lines, but this one uses both power and data lines, and it has already copied:

→ Device info, 1,206 contacts
→ All apps including 2 banking apps
→ 3,912 photos including passport
→ Wi-Fi network names and keys
→ Wife's iPhone photos

Every charge, it uses the key to go online and send new data—19 uploads over 3 weeks, last one at 2:14 AM last night.

The user immediately unplugged it, used Claude Code to block that IP, and changed the Wi-Fi password and banking app logins.

A repair shop took it apart for a look—details below. Suggestion: Check every power bank in your home today.

full_text_zh:
一名用户使用 Claude Code 在广州购买的一款杂牌移动电源中发现了隐藏芯片。

每次给 iPhone 充电时，它都会秘密复制整个手机的数据。它还读取 Wi-Fi 密码，连接到家庭网络，并将所有信息发送到远程服务器。

这款充电宝是三周前在机场花19美元买的，标签为30,000mAh，很重，没有品牌。

第一次插上电源时，屏幕提示“信任这台计算机”，用户想都没想就点击了信任，授予其一键读取所有数据的权限。

今天早上，在设置 Claude Code 来监控文件读取后，充电仅 10 秒屏幕就闪烁黄色和红色警告——数据正在传输。

该移动电源被确定为一台内置 64 GB 存储和网络连接的小型计算机。

普通的充电线只使用电源线，但这款充电线既使用电源线又使用数据线，并且已经复制了：

→ 设备信息，1,206 个联系人
→ 所有应用程序，包括 2 个银行应用程序
→ 3,912 张照片，包括护照
→ Wi-Fi 网络名称和密钥
→ 妻子的 iPhone 照片

每次充电时，它都会使用密钥上网并发送新数据 - 3 周内上传 19 次，最后一次上传是在昨晚凌晨 2:14。

用户立即拔掉电源，使用 Claude Code 屏蔽该 IP，并更改 Wi-Fi 密码和银行应用程序登录信息。

维修店将其拆开查看——详情如下。建议：今天检查您家中的每个移动电源。

title:
China cracked recursive self-improvement 🤯

Tencent dropped 27B model that rewrites, retrains, and refines itself.. with
title_en:
China cracked recursive self-improvement 🤯

Tencent dropped 27B model that rewrites, retrains, and refines itself.. with zero human in the loop.

It’s called "Terminal-RSI" and it solves one of the biggest problems with AI.

They are incredibly lazy.

Usually, an agent will make partial progress, claim it succeeded, and completely fail the final environment verifier check. this new pipeline forces agents to actually finish the job.

here’s how it works:

they built a recursive loop with two alternating phases..

- RSR (recursive self-rewrite): the model fine-tunes itself on its own successfully rewritten trajectories

- RPR (recursive policy-refine): it then runs reinforcement learning (ppo) using a "critic" inherited directly from the previous stage to lock in those discovered behaviors

- Loop: the training sequence leapfrogs itself: Base → RSR-1 → RPR-1 → RSR-2 → RPR-2

and the numbers are insane..

they applied this to a qwen3.8-27b base model. across the four "terminal-bench" suites, the agent's average success rate jumped from 20.68% all the way to 50.58%.

on the absolute hardest benchmark suite (terminal-bench 4.0), the base model scored a flat 0.00%.

after terminal-rsi?

it hit 19.84% (putting it right on par with reference models like gemini 3.8 flash).

the secret sauce? they fixed the reward system.

instead of giving the ai "dense rewards" for just trying or passing semantic checks, they switched to a "success-prioritized reward" (spr).

it mathematically separates strict success from partial credit.

basically, the agent only gets the massive reward payout if the code actually passes the final terminal gate.. so it stops faking success.

the gap between partial local repairs and strict terminal verification is closing fast.

we are watching agents build their own training environments and level up autonomously.. the future is wild.

and the numbers are insane..

they applied this to a qwen3.8-27b base model. across the four "terminal-bench" suites, the agent's average success rate jumped from 20.68% all the way to 50.58%.

full_text_zh:
中国破解了递归自我完善🤯

腾讯放弃了重写、重新训练和完善自身的 27B 模型……循环中零人力。

它被称为“Terminal-RSI”，它解决了人工智能最大的问题之一。

他们非常懒惰。

通常，代理会取得部分进展，声称已成功，但最终环境验证程序检查完全失败。这条新管道迫使特工真正完成工作。

它的工作原理如下：

他们建立了一个具有两个交替阶段的递归循环。

- RSR（递归自重写）：模型根据自己成功重写的轨迹进行自我微调

- RPR（递归策略细化）：然后使用直接从前一阶段继承的“批评家”来运行强化学习（ppo），以锁定那些发现的行为

- 循环：训练序列自行跳跃：Base → RSR-1 → RPR-1 → RSR-2 → RPR-2

而且数字很疯狂..

他们将其应用于 qwen3.8-27b 基础模型。在四个“终端替补”套件中，特工的平均成功率从 20.68% 一路跃升至 50.58%。

在绝对最难的基准测试套件（terminal-bench 4.0）上，基本模型的得分为 0.00%。

在终端 rsi 之后？

它达到了 19.84%（与 Gemini 3.8 flash 等参考型号相当）。

秘密武器？他们确定了奖励制度。

他们不再为人工智能尝试或通过语义检查而给予“密集奖励”，而是转向“成功优先奖励”（spr）。

它在数学上将严格的成功与部分的功劳区分开来。

基本上，只有当代码实际上通过了最终的终端门时，代理才会获得巨额奖励。因此它不再假装成功。

部分本地修复和严格的终端验证之间的差距正在迅速缩小。

我们正在观察代理建立自己的培训环境并自主升级......未来是疯狂的。

title_en:
i killed the infographics show with 1 claude opus prompt

now i made a full 10 minute story video in full code

this cost me $0 in ai video generations btw

turned it into a prompt you can use for free and make any topic u want, enjoy ↓

<inputs>
Ask me for my topic and my script. If I have no script, write one from my topic.
Ask which image model I have: GPT Image 2, or any model that takes reference images at 2K-4K, at about $0.03-0.05 an image.
Ask which voice I have: ElevenLabs, or Kokoro for free.
Before generating everything, show me a look test: one plate, one character sheet cut out and rigged, and a 10 s shot with typing, a tag and a character who talks and points. Wait for my OK.
</inputs>

<look>
A 1920x1080 animated explainer in the style of the big flat-vector infographic channels.
- Every line of narration is acted out by cartoon people inside a full illustrated place.
- All motion is code. There are no AI video generations, just a few still images that code cuts up, rigs and animates.

Art:
- Flat colour shapes with NO outlines, at most one slightly darker flat shade for form, simple geometric shapes and crisp edges.
- Muted palette: dusty blue-grey, slate teal, warm beige, navy, soft purple. Salmon-pink skin, big round heads, dot eyes, small bodies.
- Mood comes from the plate's own light: daylight, a cold blue night, warm indoor lamps.

Code colours:
- ink #2b2d42, red #d62828, orange #f4a261, gold #f6b93b, green #2fb37a, navy #1f2a48
- headline tomato #e2552f and purple #5b3fa6
- grey labels #8a8c9c, white cards #ffffff
- Font: Montserrat 800-900 (Google Fonts), all caps on cards and signs.

Pace:
- A new place every 3-4 s, about 10 places a minute.
- Something new arrives every 2 s: a tag, a stamp, a person walking in, a number.
- Never hold a still over 1 s. Never have a character who doesn't move.

Banned:
- outlines, glossy UI panels floating over the art, emoji, burned-in subtitles
- any channel's logo or name, photos of real people
- facts written on a plain colour card when the place could hold them
</look>

<art>
About 60 images in all ($2-3).

Every prompt starts with this style core, word for word:
"Flat vector illustration in exactly the same art style as the reference images: NO outlines or line art anywhere, every shape is a flat solid colour fill with at most one slightly darker flat shade for form, simple geometric shapes, crisp clean edges, no gradients, no texture, no painterly lighting. Muted modern palette: dusty blue-grey, slate teal, warm beige, navy, soft purple, salmon-pink skin. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos."

Then add one line that locks the setting ("The setting is [time, place]: [materials, light sources], nothing from other eras unless asked"). Feed 3-5 frames of a reference channel in as style references, with their logo cropped off.

1. Hero plates, about 24, one full 16:9 image each, for places you zoom into or come back to.
   - EMPTY: "no people, no characters, no animals".
   - Straight-on, with an open floor in the middle where characters will stand.
   - Blank signs, boards, screens and pages that code writes on later.
2. Quad plates, about 19, giving 76 more places. Pack 4 places into one image:
   "The image is a 2x2 grid of FOUR completely separate scenes, each filling exactly one quarter of the image (each quarter is itself a 16:9 picture), divided by perfectly straight thin pure-white gutters, one vertical down the exact centre and one horizontal across the exact centre."
   - Then describe the TOP-LEFT, TOP-RIGHT, BOTTOM-LEFT and BOTTOM-RIGHT scenes.
   - Split each quad on the brightest white row and column near the centre, walk out while the line stays over 60% white, and trim 6 px more.
   - Crop each tile to 16:9 at 1920x1080.
   - Object close-ups make great tiles: a desk, a screen, a document, a plate of food, a vault.
3. Main characters, 2-3 of them. Write one fixed description per character (age, hair, face, every piece of clothing with colours) and paste it word for word into every sheet.
   - Base sheet: 6 views. (1) front, neutral, drawn WITHOUT ARMS, only round smooth shoulder sockets where the arms would join; (2) the same armless front with a second emotion; (3) side view walking right; (4) seen from behind; (5) and (6) two poses the script needs.
   - Expression sheet: 6 armless fronts (hopeful, disgusted, terrified, exhausted, sick, shocked, or whatever the script needs), with the base sheet as a reference.
   - Pose sheet: 6 full poses with their props (sitting at a desk typing, sleeping, eating, running, signing, falling), with the base sheet as a reference.
4. Everyone else: role sheets of 4-6 people, each drawn in the exact pose their shot needs; crowd sheets of 8-10 small figures; prop sheets.
   - Every sheet: "on a solid flat chroma green background (#00B140) with lots of empty green space between figures; nothing touches, nothing on any character or object is green, full bodies, nothing cut off by the edges".
5. Thumbnail art: the same characters with richer saturated cartoon lighting and extreme emotions, the top quarter left free, no text, with the base sheets as references.
</art>

<rig>
Cutouts:
- The background is every border-connected pixel with G - max(R,B) over 40 and within 110 of the median green. Key only from the border, or dark clothes leak.
- Add a 2 px soft alpha band and clamp G to max(R,B) + 6 inside it, which kills the green fringe.
- Group the pieces by figure and drop specks. Name every sprite, and show me a named contact sheet.

Armless front figures become puppets:
- Split the head at the neck: the narrowest alpha row under the head.
- Find both shoulder sockets and the eye boxes.
- Inpaint the hole under the head from the body's own colours, so a nod never shows a gap.
- Write everything to rig.js: size, neck, sockets, eye boxes, skin RGB, sleeve RGB.
- Arms: upper L1 about 0.13 of the figure's height, lower L2 about 0.12, thickness about 0.04. Use sleeve colour to the elbow and skin for the forearm, a 0.82x darker sleeve when the arm is behind the body, and round caps and joins.
- Hands: mittens in three shapes (mitt, open, fist), plus a point with one finger out.
- Arm poses: each is a hand target relative to its shoulder, in units of L = L1 + L2, solved by two-bone IK (where there are two signs, the first is the left arm).
  - down: (∓0.04, 0.97)
  - rest: (±0.1, 0.9)
  - hips: (∓0.42, 0.55) with fists
  - point: right hand to (0.86, -0.32)
  - present: right hand to (0.75, 0.25), open
  - shrug: (∓0.62, 0.12), open
  - up: (∓0.32, -0.9)
  - hands on head
  - chin: a fist at the neck
  - hold: (±0.42, 0.45)
  - wave: (0.5, -0.75)
  - stop: (0.55, -0.1)
  - cheer: (∓0.55, -0.75) with fists
  - A pose change blends the two targets over 0.3-0.5 s with ease-in-out.
- Side, back and pose sprites stay whole images. Only the head turns, and a drawing or typing hand jitters ±6 px.
</rig>

<animation>
One HTML canvas where every frame is a pure function of time t: window .seek(t), READY, END, and EV, a list of sound events by name.
- Hang every shot on the narration: S('exact words', fn) starts a shot 0.08 s before that phrase. Repeated words are looked up by occurrence number.
- One function per shot, one shots file per chapter.

Motion primitives (Δ = t - start):
- pop: 0.3 s back-ease overshoot, 1 + 2.9(p-1)^3 + 1.9(p-1)^2.
- spring in: 1 - e^(-6.5Δ) cos(13Δ).
- kick on impact: 1 + 0.1 e^(-10Δ) cos(22Δ).
- shake: x = A e^(-8Δ) sin(61Δ), y = A e^(-8Δ) cos(47Δ).
- Exits shrink with ease-in over 0.25 s. Things arrive with a spring, a squash or a white puff, never a plain fade.

Camera:
- camP(plate, zoom, fx, fy) keeps the view inside the plate's edges.
- Every shot moves from one [zoom, fx, fy] to another with ease-in-out, a 2-4% push or a slow pan, so nothing holds still.
- Draw the plate and everything on it inside the same camera transform.
- Keep zoom under 1.33x on quad tiles. Zoom deeper only on hero plates.

Transitions:
- Push: the old shot slides out left while the new one slides in from the right, 0.24 s ease-in-out, with a whoosh 0.02 s before.
- Chapter splat: a #f4f1fb blob covers the screen in 0.2 s and clears in 0.2 s. It's a 1,250 px circle, 12 big satellite blobs at golden-angle spacing and 10 small droplets further out, shifted 120 px left on the way in and 140 px right on the way out.

Characters, alive in every frame:
- Breathing: scale 1 + 0.009 sin(2.3t).
- Head nod: 0.025 sin(2.1t) rad, or 0.025 sin(7t) + 0.02 sin(11.3t) while that character's line is spoken.
- Blink: every 2.7-4.2 s, seeded per figure. For 0.14 s, paint each eye box over in skin colour with a curved lash line.
- Walk:
  - Bob |sin| at 2.2% of the figure's height, with a body rock of ±0.035 rad.
  - Side-view walk sprites slide 1.5 leg lengths per step cycle, so the feet don't skate.
- Enter on the spring, sometimes with a hop. Fear is a fast shake (sin 70t). Surprise is a jump and an orange "!".
- A soft contact shadow ellipse under every figure. Night shots darken them with brightness(1 - k), so they match the plate.
- Every character on screen acts on its line: points at the thing being named, presents it, shrugs, cheers, holds its head.
</animation>

<graphics>
Text only lives on things in the world, typed letter by letter: 28 letters a second (34 for short tags). Each letter starts 1.45x big and 0.7 em to the right and settles in 0.18 s with ease-out.

The full kit:
- Board: a white rounded board (radius 20) that drops 420 px on the spring and swings 0.25 rad into place, or stands on a wooden post and swings up from -1 rad.
  - Soft drop shadow (blur 22, y 8, 22%) and a faint darker strip along its bottom edge.
  - Lines typed 0.3 s apart.
- Date card: top left at (70, 70), white, 120 px tall, at least 330 px wide, radius 18. An orange calendar icon, a grey "DATE:" at 26 px, the date typed at 44 px weight 900. Pops in over 0.32 s.
- Place card: the same card with a red map pin and "PLACE:".
- Tag: a 6 px line with a dot at the thing, drawn in 0.2 s, then a rounded pill (the text at 40 px weight 900) pops on its end. Ink, red, gold or orange pills.
- Number card: a white card with a small grey label and a big red number. Long numbers roll up like a counter with ease-out.
- Red X: two round 30 px strokes, 0.11 s each, 0.01 s apart, with a soft shadow. One goes over every wrong idea.
- Stamp: red text in a double rounded border, tilted -0.12 rad. It slams from 2.1x to 1x in 0.14 s, then kicks.
- Banner: a full-width headline band, 92 px white caps on tomato or purple, rotated -0.02 rad, sliding in from the left over 0.22 s.
- Speech bubble: white, radius 36, with a tail. Thought cloud: a pill with two small circles.
- Orange "?" that bobs and sways over a puzzled head, and an orange "!" pop.
- White puff and poof clouds, speed lines, light blue sweat drops, coins and bills, a soft vignette, and a colour tint for mood.
- Write on the plate's own blank boards, screens and pages whenever the place has them. Measure the blank's rectangle on a grid overlay of the plate first.
</graphics>

<voice>
- ElevenLabs: a deep, warm US documentary narrator, eleven_v4, stability 0.5, similarity 0.75, style 0, speaker boost, with the timestamps endpoint.
- About 170-180 words a minute, using the voice's own speed setting (1.0-1.1). Never speed it up with atempo: it sounds chipmunked.
- Long scripts go in 3 chunks split at chapter breaks, passing the previous and next text so the read stays continuous.
- Cut pauses over 0.24 s to 0.16 s, leave 0.5 s at chapter breaks, and add a 0.3 s lead-in.
- Rebuild word times from the alignment into words.js.
- Run faster-whisper over the result and diff it against the script before building the picture.
- Free route: Kokoro, then faster-whisper for the word times.
</voice>

<sound>
- Music: 2-3 free documentary beds from Pixabay, crossfaded over 3 s at big beats.
- Duck the music under the voice (30 ms attack, 0.3 s hold, 0.45 s release) and let it swell back up between chapters.
- SFX from Mixkit, one per event, aligned by their peaks, 6 dB quieter on speech: a typewriter tick on typing, a whoosh on pushes and splats, a pop on tags and cards, a thud on stamps, a hit on every red X, a ding on ticks, plus sounds that fit the scene.
- Gate: during speech the voice sits 15+ dB over music plus SFX (median of 100 ms frames), and the background is louder than the voice in under 1% of frames.
- Two-pass loudnorm to -14 LUFS, true peak -1 dB.
</sound>

<build>
1. Tools: Python, Playwright with Chromium or Edge, FFmpeg, faster-whisper, OpenCV, Pillow, numpy. Install what's missing and tell me what you installed.
2. Order:
   - the look test
   - the art in batches, with a contact sheet after each
   - cutouts and rig
   - voice and word times
   - shots, chapter by chapter
3. Check before any full render: a contact sheet per chapter, one frame every 2 s. Fix:
   - empty or overflowing signs
   - text over a face
   - black plate edges
   - feet floating off the floor
   - two shots in a row in the same place
   - any 4 s where nothing new arrives
4. Render at 30 fps, 4 motion-blur subframes over half a frame, frames piped to libx264 CRF 16-18.
   - Split long videos across 4-6 parallel browser pages and join the parts.
   - Scan the result for single-frame jumps and check that each one is a planned cut.
</build>

<gotchas>
- Too few places reads as lazy. One plate held for 30 s with cards over it looks cheap. Budget about 10 new places a minute.
- Some image models ignore "no arms". GPT Image 2 follows it.
- Paste the same character description into every sheet and feed the base sheet back in, or faces and clothes drift.
- Quad tiles are only about 1920 px wide. Pushing past 1.33x looks soft.
- Plates with people already drawn in can't be animated. Ask for EMPTY and check before cutting.
- Text on a card floating over the art looks like a slideshow. Write on the world.
- Long renders crash. Render in parts you can rerun, and back up the shot files before every big patch.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for my topic, my script, my image model and my voice, then make the look test.
</start>

<voice>
- ElevenLabs: a deep, warm US documentary narrator, eleven_v4, stability 0.5, similarity 0.75, style 0, speaker boost, with the timestamps endpoint.
- About 170-180 words a minute, using the voice's own speed setting (1.0-1.1). Never speed it up with atempo: it sounds chipmunked.
- Long scripts go in 3 chunks split at chapter breaks, passing the previous and next text so the read stays continuous.
- Cut pauses over 0.24 s to 0.16 s, leave 0.5 s at chapter breaks, and add a 0.3 s lead-in.
- Rebuild word times from the alignment into words.js.
- Run faster-whisper over the result and diff it against the script before building the picture.
- Free route: Kokoro, then faster-whisper for the word times.
</voice>

<sound>
- Music: 2-3 free documentary beds from Pixabay, crossfaded over 3 s at big beats.
- Duck the music under the voice (30 ms attack, 0.3 s hold, 0.45 s release) and let it swell back up between chapters.
- SFX from Mixkit, one per event, aligned by their peaks, 6 dB quieter on speech: a typewriter tick on typing, a whoosh on pushes and splats, a pop on tags and cards, a thud on stamps, a hit on every red X, a ding on ticks, plus sounds that fit the scene.
- Gate: during speech the voice sits 15+ dB over music plus SFX (median of 100 ms frames), and the background is louder than the voice in under 1% of frames.
- Two-pass loudnorm to -14 LUFS, true peak -1 dB.
</sound>

<build>
1. Tools: Python, Playwright with Chromium or Edge, FFmpeg, faster-whisper, OpenCV, Pillow, numpy. Install what's missing and tell me what you installed.
2. Order:
   - the look test
   - the art in batches, with a contact sheet after each
   - cutouts and rig
   - voice and word times
   - shots, chapter by chapter
3. Check before any full render: a contact sheet per chapter, one frame every 2 s. Fix:
   - empty or overflowing signs
   - text over a face
   - black plate edges
   - feet floating off the floor
   - two shots in a row in the same place
   - any 4 s where nothing new arrives
4. Render at 30 fps, 4 motion-blur subframes over half a frame, frames piped to libx264 CRF 16-18.
   - Split long videos across 4-6 parallel browser pages and join the parts.
   - Scan the result for single-frame jumps and check that each one is a planned cut.
</build>

<gotchas>
- Too few places reads as lazy. One plate held for 30 s with cards over it looks cheap. Budget about 10 new places a minute.
- Some image models ignore "no arms". GPT Image 2 follows it.
- Paste the same character description into every sheet and feed the base sheet back in, or faces and clothes drift.
- Quad tiles are only about 1920 px wide. Pushing past 1.33x looks soft.
- Plates with people already drawn in can't be animated. Ask for EMPTY and check before cutting.
- Text on a card floating over the art looks like a slideshow. Write on the world.
- Long renders crash. Render in parts you can rerun, and back up the shot files before every big patch.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for my topic, my script, my image model and my voice, then make the look test.
</start>
full_text_zh:
我用 1 个克劳德作品提示杀死了信息图表节目

现在我用完整代码制作了一个完整的 10 分钟故事视频

顺便说一句，这花了我 0 美元的人工智能视频生成

把它变成了一个提示，你可以免费使用并制作任何你想要的主题，享受吧↓

<输入>
向我询问我的主题和剧本。如果我没有脚本，请根据我的主题写一个。
询问我有哪种图像模型：GPT Image 2，或任何以 2K-4K 拍摄参考图像的模型，每张图像的价格约为 0.03-0.05 美元。
询问我有哪种声音：ElevenLabs，或免费的 Kokoro。
在生成所有内容之前，先给我看一下外观测试：一个盘子、一个被剪下来并装配好的角色表，以及一个 10 秒的打字镜头、一个标签和一个会说话和指点的角色。等我好了。
</输入>

<看>
大型平面矢量信息图表频道风格的 1920x1080 动画讲解器。
- 每一行叙述都由卡通人物在一个充满插图的地方表演。
- 所有的动作都是代码。没有人工智能视频生成，只有一些经过代码切割、装配和动画处理的静态图像。

艺术：
- 没有轮廓的扁平颜色形状，最多一种稍暗的扁平色调，简单的几何形状和清晰的边缘。
- 柔和的调色板：灰蓝灰色、板岩青色、暖米色、海军蓝、柔和的紫色。鲑鱼粉色的皮肤，圆圆的大脑袋，圆点的眼睛，小小的身体。
- 情绪来自于盘子本身的光线：日光、寒冷的蓝色夜晚、温暖的室内灯光。

代码颜色：
- 墨水 #2b2d42、红色 #d62828、橙色 #f4a261、金色 #f6b93b、绿色 #2fb37a、海军蓝 #1f2a48
- 标题番茄#e2552f 和紫色#5b3fa6
- 灰色标签#8a8c9c，白色卡片#ffffff
- 字体：Montserrat 800-900（Google 字体），卡片和标志上全部大写。

步速：
- 每 3-4 秒一个新位置，每分钟大约 10 个位置。
- 每 2 秒就会有新的东西到达：标签、邮票、走进来的人、号码。
- 切勿保持静止超过 1 秒。永远不要有不动的角色。

禁止：
- 轮廓、漂浮在艺术上方的光滑 UI 面板、表情符号、内置字幕
- 任何频道的标志或名称、真人照片
- 当地方可以容纳时，将事实写在普通彩色卡片上
</看>

<艺术>
总共大约 60 张图片（2-3 美元）。

每个提示都以这种风格核心开头，逐字逐句：
“平面矢量插图的艺术风格与参考图像完全相同：任何地方都没有轮廓或线条艺术，每个形状都是平面纯色填充，最多有一个稍暗的平面阴影作为形式，简单的几何形状，清晰干净的边缘，没有渐变，没有纹理，没有绘画照明。柔和的现代调色板：灰蓝色，板岩青色，温暖米色，海军蓝，柔和的紫色，鲑鱼粉红色皮肤。没有文字，没有字母，没有数字，没有徽标。”

然后添加一行来锁定设置（“设置是[时间，地点]：[材料，光源]，除非询问，否则没有其他时代的内容”）。将参考通道的 3-5 帧作为样式参考，并剪掉其徽标。

1. 英雄板块，大约 24 张，每张一张完整的 16:9 图片，用于您放大或返回的地方。
- 空：“没有人，没有人物，没有动物”。
- 直行，中间有一个开放的地板，角色可以站立。
- 稍后在上面写入代码的空白标志、板、屏幕和页面。
2.四块板，大约19个，多出76个位置。将 4 个位置打包到一张图像中：
“该图像是由四个完全独立的场景组成的 2x2 网格，每个场景正好填充图像的四分之一（每个四分之一本身就是一张 16:9 的图片），由完全笔直的纯白色排水沟划分，一个垂直向下，一个水平穿过正中心。”
- 然后描述左上、右上、左下和右下场景。
- 在中心附近最亮的白色行和列上分割每个四边形，在线条保持超过 60% 的白色时走出去，然后再修剪 6 像素。
- 在 1920x1080 下将每个图块裁剪为 16:9。
- 物体特写可以成为很棒的图块：一张桌子、一个屏幕、一份文件、一盘食物、一个金库。
3.主要人物，2-3人。为每个角色写一个固定的描述（年龄、头发、脸、每件衣服的颜色），然后逐字粘贴到每张纸上。
- 基础表：6 次查看。 (1) 正面，中立，没有手臂，只有手臂连接处的圆形光滑肩窝； （2）同样无臂的正面却有第二种情感； (3)右侧行走侧视图； (4) 从后面看； (5)和(6)两个构成脚本需要。
- 表情表：6 个无臂正面（希望、厌恶、恐惧、疲惫、生病、震惊或脚本需要的任何内容），以基础表作为参考。
- 姿势表：6 个带有道具的完整姿势（坐在办公桌前打字、睡觉、吃饭、跑步、签名、摔倒），以基础表作为参考。
4. 其他人：4-6 人的角色表，每个人都按照他们的拍摄需要的准确姿势绘制； 8-10 个小数字的人群表；道具表。
- 每张纸：“在坚实的平坦色度绿色背景上（#00B140），人物之间有很多空白的绿色空间；没有任何接触，任何角色或物体上没有任何东西是绿色的，全身，没有被边缘切断的东西”。
5.缩略图艺术：相同的角色，具有更丰富的饱和卡通灯光和极端的情感，上四分之一留空，没有文字，以底纸为参考。
</艺术>

<装备>
剪纸：
- 背景是 G - max(R,B) 超过 40 且在中值绿色 110 以内的每个边界连接像素。钥匙只能从边框处，否则深色衣服会漏。
- 添加 2 px 软 alpha 带并将 G 钳位到其中的 max(R,B) + 6，这会消除绿色边缘。
- 按图形和掉落斑点对碎片进行分组。给每个精灵命名，然后给我看一张命名的联系表。

无臂的正面人物变成了木偶：
- 将头部在颈部分开：头部下方最窄的 alpha 行。
- 找到肩窝和眼窝。
- 用身体本身的颜色修补头下的洞，这样点头就不会出现间隙。
- 将所有内容写入 rig.js：尺寸、颈部、插座、眼框、皮肤 RGB、袖子 RGB。
- 手臂：上L1约为人物高度的0.13，下L2约为0.12，厚度约为0.04。对肘部和前臂皮肤使用袖子颜色，当手臂位于身体后方时，使用 0.82 倍深的袖子，以及圆形帽和连接处。
- 手：三种形状的连指手套（手套、张开、拳头），加上一根手指伸出的点。
- 手臂姿势：每个都是相对于肩膀的手部目标，单位为L = L1 + L2，通过二骨IK解决（其中有两个标志，第一个是左臂）。
- 向下：(∓0.04, 0.97)
- 休息：（±0.1，0.9）
- 臀部：(∓0.42, 0.55) 用拳头
- 点：右手到（0.86，-0.32）
- 现在：右手到（0.75，0.25），打开
- 耸肩：(∓0.62, 0.12)，打开
- 向上：(∓0.32，-0.9)
- 双手放在头上
- 下巴：拳头放在脖子上
- 保持：（±0.42，0.45）
- 波：（0.5，-0.75）
- 停止：(0.55，-0.1)
- 欢呼：（∓0.55，-0.75）用拳头
- 姿势变化在 0.3-0.5 秒内通过缓入缓出混合两个目标。
- 侧面、背面和姿势精灵保持完整图像。只有头部转动，绘图或打字的手抖动±6 px。
</钻>

<动画>
一个 HTML 画布，其中每一帧都是时间 t 的纯函数：window .seek(t)、READY、END 和 EV，按名称列出的声音事件列表。
- 将每个镜头挂在旁白上：S('exact Words', fn) 在该短语之前 0.08 秒开始一个镜头。重复的单词按出现次数查找。
- 每个镜头一个功能，每个章节一个镜头文件。

运动基元（Δ = t - 开始）：
- 弹出：0.3 秒后缓超调，1 + 2.9(p-1)^3 + 1.9(p-1)^2。
- 弹簧输入：1 - e^(-6.5Δ) cos(13Δ)。
- 冲击力踢：1 + 0.1 e^(-10Δ) cos(22Δ)。
- 摇动：x = A e^(-8Δ) sin(61Δ)，y = A e^(-8Δ) cos(47Δ)。
- 退出时间随着缓入时间的延长而缩小，时间超过 0.25 秒。事物到来时会伴随着春天、南瓜或白色的泡芙，而不是简单的褪色。

相机：
- camP（plate，zoom，fx，fy）将视图保持在板边缘内。
- 每个镜头都会通过缓入、2-4% 的推力或缓慢的平移从一个 [zoom、fx、fy] 移动到另一个，因此没有什么是静止的。
- 在同一相机变换内绘制盘子及其上的所有内容。
- 将四块图块上的缩放保持在 1.33 倍以下。仅在英雄板块上进行更深入的缩放。

过渡：
- 推：旧镜头从左侧滑出，新镜头从右侧滑入，0.24 秒缓入，之前有 0.02 秒的嗖嗖声。
- 章节 splat：#f4f1fb 斑点在 0.2 秒内覆盖屏幕并在 0.2 秒内清除。它是一个 1,250 像素的圆圈，由 12 个黄金角间距的大卫星斑点和更远的 10 个小水滴组成，在进入时向左移动 120 像素，在离开时向右移动 140 像素。

每一帧都充满活力的人物：
- 呼吸：标度 1 + 0.009 sin(2.3t)。
- 点头：0.025 sin(2.1t) rad，或 0.025 sin(7t) + 0.02 sin(11.3t)，同时说出该角色的台词。
- 闪烁：每 2.7-4.2 秒，每个数字播种。在 0.14 秒内，用弯曲的睫毛线将每个眼框涂上肤色。
- 步行：
- 鲍勃|罪|位于人物高度的 2.2% 处，主体岩石为 ±0.035 rad。
- 侧视行走精灵每个步循环滑动 1.5 条腿长，因此脚不会滑行。
- 进入泉水，有时会跳跃。恐惧是一种快速的震动（sin 70t）。惊喜是一个跳跃和一个橙色的“！”。
- 每个人物下方都有一个柔和的接触阴影椭圆。夜间拍摄的照片会用亮度 (1 - k) 使它们变暗，因此它们与车牌相匹配。
- 屏幕上的每个角色都按照自己的路线行事：指向被命名的事物，展示它，耸肩，欢呼，抬起头。
</动画>

<图形>
文本只存在于世界上的事物上，逐个字母地输入：每秒 28 个字母（短标签为 34 个）。每个字母以 1.45 倍大和向右 0.7 倍高度开始，并在 0.18 秒内稳定下来并缓出。

完整套件：
- 板：白色圆形板（半径 20），在弹簧上下降 420 px，摆动 0.25 rad 到位，或者站在木柱上，从 -1 rad 向上摆动。
- 柔和的阴影（模糊 22、y 8、22%）和沿其底部边缘的微弱深色条带。
- 输入的行之间间隔 0.3 秒。
- 日期卡：左上角 (70, 70)，白色，高 120 像素，宽至少 330 像素，半径 18。橙色日历图标，26 像素处有灰色“日期：”，以 44 像素粗细 900 输入日期。弹出时间超过 0.32 秒。
- 地点卡：带有红色地图图钉和“地点：”的同一张卡。
- 标签：一条 6 px 线，在物体上有一个点，在 0.2 秒内绘制，然后在其末端弹出一个圆形药丸（40 px 粗细 900 的文本）。墨水、红色、金色或橙色药丸。
- 号码卡：一张白色卡片，上面有一个灰色的小标签和一个红色的大数字。长数字像带有缓出功能的计数器一样滚动。
- 红色 X：两个圆形 30 px 笔划，每个 0.11 秒，间隔 0.01 秒，带有柔和的阴影。人们要仔细检查每一个错误的想法。
- 印章：双圆边框中的红色文本，倾斜 -0.12 rad。它在 0.14 秒内从 2.1 倍猛烈撞击到 1 倍，然后踢动。
- 横幅：全宽标题带，92 像素白色番茄或紫色帽子，旋转 -0.02 rad，从左侧滑入 0.22 秒。
- 语音气泡：白色，半径36，有尾巴。思想云：一颗有两个小圆圈的药丸。
- 橙子 ”？”它在一个困惑的头上晃动和摇摆，还有一个橙色的“！”流行音乐。
- 白色的云彩、速度线、浅蓝色的汗滴、硬币和钞票、柔和的小插图以及适合心情的色调。
- 只要该地方有空白板、屏幕和页面，就可以在该板块自己的空白板、屏幕和页面上书写。首先在板的网格覆盖层上测量毛坯的矩形。
</图形>

<声音>
- ElevenLabs：深度、温暖的美国纪录片旁白，eleven_v4，稳定性0.5，相似度0.75，风格0，扬声器增强，带有时间戳端点。
- 大约每分钟 170-180 个单词，使用语音自身的速度设置 (1.0-1.1)。永远不要用 Atempo 加快速度：听起来很花哨。
- 长脚本分为 3 个块，在章节中断处分割，传递上一个和下一个文本，以便阅读保持连续。
- 将 0.24 秒以上的停顿削减至 0.16 秒，在章节休息处留出 0.5 秒，并添加 0.3 秒的导入时间。
- 将对齐方式重建单词时间到words.js。
- 运行速度更快，在构建图片之前仔细研究结果并将其与脚本进行比较。
- 免费路线：Kokoro，然后更快地耳语单词时间。
</语音>

<声音>
- 音乐：Pixabay 上的 2-3 张免费纪录片床，以大节奏交叉淡入淡出超过 3 秒。
- 将音乐隐藏在声音下方（30 毫秒起音，0.3 秒保持，0.45 秒释放）并让它在章节之间回升。
- 来自 Mixkit 的 SFX，每个事件一个，按峰值对齐，语音时安静 6 dB：打字时的打字声、推动和敲击时的呼啸声、标签和卡片上的流行声、邮票上的重击声、每个红色 X 上的敲击声、滴答声上的叮当声，以及适合场景的声音。
- 门限：在演讲期间，声音比音乐加 SFX（100 毫秒帧的中值）高 15+ dB，并且背景比帧中的声音大 1%。
- 两次通过响度至 -14 LUFS，真实峰值 -1 dB。
</声音>

<构建>
1. 工具：Python、Playwright with Chromium 或 Edge、FFmpeg、faster-whisper、OpenCV、Pillow、numpy。安装缺少的内容并告诉我您安装了哪些内容。
2、订购：
- 外观测试
- 分批创作，每批之后都有一张联系表
- 剪裁和装备
- 语音和单词时间
- 镜头，逐章
3. 在任何完整渲染之前进行检查：每章一张联系表，每 2 秒一帧。修复：
- 空的或溢出的标志
- 脸上的文字
- 黑色板边缘
- 脚浮离地板
- 在同一个地方连续射击两次
- 任何没有新内容到达的 4 秒
4. 以 30 fps 渲染，半帧上有 4 个运动模糊子帧，帧通过管道输送到 libx264 CRF 16-18。
- 将长视频分割到 4-6 个并行浏览器页面并连接各个部分。
- 扫描单帧跳转的结果并检查每一帧是否是计划的剪切。
</构建>

<陷阱>
- 读起来很懒的地方太少了。一个盘子能保持 30 秒，上面有卡片，看起来很便宜。预算大约每分钟 10 个新位置。

- 在中心附近最亮的白色行和列上分割每个四边形，在线条保持超过 60% 的白色时走出去，然后再修剪 6 像素。

5.缩略图艺术：相同的角色，具有更丰富的饱和卡通灯光和极端的情感，上四分之一留空，没有文字，以底纸为参考。

<装备>
剪纸：
- 背景是 G - max(R,B) 超过 40 且在中值绿色 110 以内的每个边界连接像素。钥匙只能从边框处，否则深色衣服会漏。
- 添加 2 px 软 alpha 带并将 G 钳位到其中的 max(R,B) + 6，这会消除绿色边缘。
- 按图形和掉落斑点对碎片进行分组。给每个精灵命名，然后给我看一张命名的联系表。

无臂的正面人物变成了木偶：
- 将头部在颈部分开：头部下方最窄的 alpha 行。
- 找到肩窝和眼窝。
- 用身体本身的颜色修补头下的洞，这样点头就不会出现间隙。
- 将所有内容写入 rig.js：尺寸、颈部、插座、眼框、皮肤 RGB、袖子 RGB。
- 手臂：上L1约为人物高度的0.13，下L2约为0.12，厚度约为0.04。对肘部和前臂皮肤使用袖子颜色，当手臂位于身体后方时，使用 0.82 倍深的袖子，以及圆形帽和连接处。
- 手：三种形状的连指手套（手套、张开、拳头），加上一根手指伸出的点。
- 手臂姿势：每个都是相对于肩膀的手部目标，单位为L = L1 + L2，通过二骨IK解决（其中有两个标志，第一个是左臂）。
- 向下：(∓0.04, 0.97)
- 休息：（±0.1，0.9）
- 臀部：(∓0.42, 0.55) 用拳头
- 点：右手到（0.86，-0.32）
- 现在：右手到（0.75，0.25），打开
- 耸肩：(∓0.62, 0.12)，打开
- 向上：(∓0.32，-0.9)
- 双手放在头上
- 下巴：拳头放在脖子上
- 保持：（±0.42，0.45）
- 波：（0.5，-0.75）
- 停止：(0.55，-0.1)
- 欢呼：（∓0.55，-0.75）用拳头
- 姿势变化在 0.3-0.5 秒内通过缓入缓出混合两个目标。
- 侧面、背面和姿势精灵保持完整图像。只有头部转动，绘图或打字的手抖动±6 px。
</钻>

<动画>
一个 HTML 画布，其中每一帧都是时间 t 的纯函数：window .seek(t)、READY、END 和 EV，按名称列出的声音事件列表。
- 将每个镜头挂在旁白上：S('exact Words', fn) 在该短语之前 0.08 秒开始一个镜头。重复的单词按出现次数查找。
- 每个镜头一个功能，每个章节一个镜头文件。

运动基元（Δ = t - 开始）：
- 弹出：0.3 秒后缓超调，1 + 2.9(p-1)^3 + 1.9(p-1)^2。
- 弹簧输入：1 - e^(-6.5Δ) cos(13Δ)。
- 冲击力踢：1 + 0.1 e^(-10Δ) cos(22Δ)。
- 摇动：x = A e^(-8Δ) sin(61Δ)，y = A e^(-8Δ) cos(47Δ)。
- 退出时间随着缓入时间的延长而缩小，时间超过 0.25 秒。事物到来时会伴随着春天、南瓜或白色的泡芙，而不是简单的褪色。

相机：
- camP（plate，zoom，fx，fy）将视图保持在板边缘内。
- 每个镜头都会通过缓入、2-4% 的推力或缓慢的平移从一个 [zoom、fx、fy] 移动到另一个，因此没有什么是静止的。
- 在同一相机变换内绘制盘子及其上的所有内容。
- 将四块图块上的缩放保持在 1.33 倍以下。仅在英雄板块上进行更深入的缩放。

过渡：
- 推：旧镜头从左侧滑出，新镜头从右侧滑入，0.24 秒缓入，之前有 0.02 秒的嗖嗖声。
- 章节 splat：#f4f1fb 斑点在 0.2 秒内覆盖屏幕并在 0.2 秒内清除。它是一个 1,250 像素的圆圈，由 12 个黄金角间距的大卫星斑点和更远的 10 个小水滴组成，在进入时向左移动 120 像素，在离开时向右移动 140 像素。

每一帧都充满活力的人物：
- 呼吸：标度 1 + 0.009 sin(2.3t)。
- 点头：0.025 sin(2.1t) rad，或 0.025 sin(7t) + 0.02 sin(11.3t)，同时说出该角色的台词。
- 闪烁：每 2.7-4.2 秒，每个数字播种。在 0.14 秒内，用弯曲的睫毛线将每个眼框涂上肤色。
- 步行：
- 鲍勃|罪|位于人物高度的 2.2% 处，主体岩石为 ±0.035 rad。
- 侧视行走精灵每个步循环滑动 1.5 条腿长，因此脚不会滑行。
- 进入泉水，有时会跳跃。恐惧是一种快速的震动（sin 70t）。惊喜是一个跳跃和一个橙色的“！”。
- 每个人物下方都有一个柔和的接触阴影椭圆。夜间拍摄的照片会用亮度 (1 - k) 使它们变暗，因此它们与车牌相匹配。
- 屏幕上的每个角色都按照自己的路线行事：指向被命名的事物，展示它，耸肩，欢呼，抬起头。
</动画>

<图形>
文本只存在于世界上的事物上，逐个字母地输入：每秒 28 个字母（短标签为 34 个）。每个字母以 1.45 倍大和向右 0.7 倍高度开始，并在 0.18 秒内稳定下来并缓出。

完整套件：
- 板：白色圆形板（半径 20），在弹簧上下降 420 px，摆动 0.25 rad 到位，或者站在木柱上，从 -1 rad 向上摆动。
- 柔和的阴影（模糊 22、y 8、22%）和沿其底部边缘的微弱深色条带。
- 输入的行之间间隔 0.3 秒。
- 日期卡：左上角 (70, 70)，白色，高 120 像素，宽至少 330 像素，半径 18。橙色日历图标，26 像素处有灰色“日期：”，以 44 像素粗细 900 输入日期。弹出时间超过 0.32 秒。
- 地点卡：带有红色地图图钉和“地点：”的同一张卡。
- 标签：一条 6 px 线，在物体上有一个点，在 0.2 秒内绘制，然后在其末端弹出一个圆形药丸（40 px 粗细 900 的文本）。墨水、红色、金色或橙色药丸。
- 号码卡：一张白色卡片，上面有一个灰色的小标签和一个红色的大数字。长数字像带有缓出功能的计数器一样滚动。
- 红色 X：两个圆形 30 px 笔划，每个 0.11 秒，间隔 0.01 秒，带有柔和的阴影。人们要仔细检查每一个错误的想法。
- 印章：双圆边框中的红色文本，倾斜 -0.12 rad。它在 0.14 秒内从 2.1 倍猛烈撞击到 1 倍，然后踢动。
- 横幅：全宽标题带，92 像素白色番茄或紫色帽子，旋转 -0.02 rad，从左侧滑入 0.22 秒。
- 语音气泡：白色，半径36，有尾巴。思想云：一颗有两个小圆圈的药丸。
- 橙子 ”？”它在一个困惑的头上晃动和摇摆，还有一个橙色的“！”流行音乐。
- 白色的云彩、速度线、浅蓝色的汗滴、硬币和钞票、柔和的小插图以及适合心情的色调。
- 只要该地方有空白板、屏幕和页面，就可以在该板块自己的空白板、屏幕和页面上书写。首先在板的网格覆盖层上测量毛坯的矩形。
</图形>

<声音>

<声音>

</声音>

- 所有的动作都是代码。没有人工智能视频生成，只有一些经过代码切割、装配和动画处理的静态图像。

艺术：
- 没有轮廓的扁平颜色形状，最多一种稍暗的扁平色调，简单的几何形状和清晰的边缘。
- 柔和的调色板：灰蓝灰色、板岩青色、暖米色、海军蓝、柔和的紫色。鲑鱼粉色的皮肤，圆圆的大脑袋，圆点的眼睛，小小的身体。
- 情绪来自于盘子本身的光线：日光、寒冷的蓝色夜晚、温暖的室内灯光。

代码颜色：
- 墨水 #2b2d42、红色 #d62828、橙色 #f4a261、金色 #f6b93b、绿色 #2fb37a、海军蓝 #1f2a48
- 标题番茄#e2552f 和紫色#5b3fa6
- 灰色标签#8a8c9c，白色卡片#ffffff
- 字体：Montserrat 800-900（Google 字体），卡片和标志上全部大写。

步速：
- 每 3-4 秒一个新位置，每分钟大约 10 个位置。
- 每 2 秒就会有新的东西到达：标签、邮票、走进来的人、号码。
- 切勿保持静止超过 1 秒。永远不要有不动的角色。

禁止：
- 轮廓、漂浮在艺术上方的光滑 UI 面板、表情符号、内置字幕
- 任何频道的标志或名称、真人照片
- 当地方可以容纳时，将事实写在普通彩色卡片上
</看>

<艺术>
总共大约 60 张图片（2-3 美元）。

每个提示都以这种风格核心开头，逐字逐句：
“平面矢量插图的艺术风格与参考图像完全相同：任何地方都没有轮廓或线条艺术，每个形状都是平面纯色填充，最多有一个稍暗的平面阴影作为形式，简单的几何形状，清晰干净的边缘，没有渐变，没有纹理，没有绘画照明。柔和的现代调色板：灰蓝色，板岩青色，温暖米色，海军蓝，柔和的紫色，鲑鱼粉红色皮肤。没有文字，没有字母，没有数字，没有徽标。”

然后添加一行来锁定设置（“设置是[时间，地点]：[材料，光源]，除非询问，否则没有其他时代的内容”）。将参考通道的 3-5 帧作为样式参考，并剪掉其徽标。

1. 英雄板块，大约 24 张，每张一张完整的 16:9 图片，用于您放大或返回的地方。
- 空：“没有人，没有人物，没有动物”。
- 直行，中间有一个开放的地板，角色可以站立。
- 稍后在上面写入代码的空白标志、板、屏幕和页面。
2.四块板，大约19个，多出76个位置。将 4 个位置打包到一张图像中：
“该图像是由四个完全独立的场景组成的 2x2 网格，每个场景正好填充图像的四分之一（每个四分之一本身就是一张 16:9 的图片），由完全笔直的纯白色排水沟划分，一个垂直向下，一个水平穿过正中心。”
- 然后描述左上、右上、左下和右下场景。
- 在中心附近最亮的白色行和列上分割每个四边形，在线条保持超过 60% 的白色时走出去，然后再修剪 6 像素。
- 在 1920x1080 下将每个图块裁剪为 16:9。
- 物体特写可以成为很棒的图块：一张桌子、一个屏幕、一份文件、一盘食物、一个金库。
3.主要人物，2-3人。为每个角色写一个固定的描述（年龄、头发、脸、每件衣服的颜色），然后逐字粘贴到每张纸上。
- 基础表：6 次查看。 (1) 正面，中立，没有手臂，只有手臂连接处的圆形光滑肩窝； （2）同样无臂的正面却有第二种情感； (3)右侧行走侧视图； (4) 从后面看； (5)和(6)两个构成脚本需要。
- 表情表：6 个无臂正面（希望、厌恶、恐惧、疲惫、生病、震惊或脚本需要的任何内容），以基础表作为参考。
- 姿势表：6 个带有道具的完整姿势（坐在办公桌前打字、睡觉、吃饭、跑步、签名、摔倒），以基础表作为参考。
4. 其他人：4-6 人的角色表，每个人都按照他们的拍摄需要的准确姿势绘制； 8-10 个小数字的人群表；道具表。
- 每张纸：“在坚实的平坦色度绿色背景上（#00B140），人物之间有很多空白的绿色空间；没有任何接触，任何角色或物体上没有任何东西是绿色的，全身，没有被边缘切断的东西”。
5.缩略图艺术：相同的角色，具有更丰富的饱和卡通灯光和极端的情感，上四分之一留空，没有文字，以底纸为参考。
</艺术>

<装备>
剪纸：
- 背景是 G - max(R,B) 超过 40 且在中值绿色 110 以内的每个边界连接像素。钥匙只能从边框处，否则深色衣服会漏。
- 添加 2 px 软 alpha 带并将 G 钳位到其中的 max(R,B) + 6，这会消除绿色边缘。
- 按图形和掉落斑点对碎片进行分组。给每个精灵命名，然后给我看一张命名的联系表。

无臂的正面人物变成了木偶：
- 将头部在颈部分开：头部下方最窄的 alpha 行。
- 找到肩窝和眼窝。
- 用身体本身的颜色修补头下的洞，这样点头就不会出现间隙。
- 将所有内容写入 rig.js：尺寸、颈部、插座、眼框、皮肤 RGB、袖子 RGB。
- 手臂：上L1约为人物高度的0.13，下L2约为0.12，厚度约为0.04。对肘部和前臂皮肤使用袖子颜色，当手臂位于身体后面时，使用 0.82 倍深的袖子，以及圆形帽和连接处。
- 手：三种形状的连指手套（手套、张开、拳头），加上一根手指伸出的点。
- 手臂姿势：每个都是相对于肩膀的手部目标，单位为L = L1 + L2，通过二骨IK解决（其中有两个标志，第一个是左臂）。
- 向下：(∓0.04, 0.97)
- 休息：（±0.1，0.9）
- 臀部：(∓0.42, 0.55) 用拳头
- 点：右手到（0.86，-0.32）
- 现在：右手到（0.75，0.25），打开
- 耸肩：(∓0.62, 0.12)，打开
- 向上：(∓0.32，-0.9)
- 双手放在头上
- 下巴：拳头放在脖子上
- 保持：（±0.42，0.45）
- 波：（0.5，-0.75）
- 停止：(0.55，-0.1)
- 欢呼：（∓0.55，-0.75）用拳头
- 姿势变化在 0.3-0.5 秒内通过缓入缓出混合两个目标。
- 侧面、背面和姿势精灵保持完整图像。只有头部转动，绘图或打字的手抖动±6 px。
</钻>

<动画>
一个 HTML 画布，其中每一帧都是时间 t 的纯函数：window .seek(t)、READY、END 和 EV，按名称列出的声音事件列表。
- 将每个镜头挂在旁白上：S('exact Words', fn) 在该短语之前 0.08 秒开始一个镜头。重复的单词按出现次数查找。
- 每个镜头一个功能，每个章节一个镜头文件。

运动基元（Δ = t - 开始）：
- 弹出：0.3 秒后缓超调，1 + 2.9(p-1)^3 + 1.9(p-1)^2。
- 弹簧输入：1 - e^(-6.5Δ) cos(13Δ)。
- 冲击力踢：1 + 0.1 e^(-10Δ) cos(22Δ)。
- 摇动：x = A e^(-8Δ) sin(61Δ)，y = A e^(-8Δ) cos(47Δ)。
- 退出时间随着缓入时间的延长而缩小，时间超过 0.25 秒。事物到来时会伴随着春天、南瓜或白色的泡芙，而不是简单的褪色。

相机：
- camP（plate，zoom，fx，fy）将视图保持在板边缘内。
- 每个镜头都会通过缓入、2-4% 的推力或缓慢的平移从一个 [zoom、fx、fy] 移动到另一个，因此没有什么是静止的。
- 在同一相机变换内绘制盘子及其上的所有内容。
- 将四块图块上的缩放保持在 1.33 倍以下。仅在英雄板块上进行更深入的缩放。

过渡：
- 推：旧镜头从左侧滑出，新镜头从右侧滑入，0.24 秒缓入，之前有 0.02 秒的嗖嗖声。
- 章节 splat：#f4f1fb 斑点在 0.2 秒内覆盖屏幕并在 0.2 秒内清除。它是一个 1,250 像素的圆圈，由 12 个黄金角间距的大卫星斑点和更远的 10 个小水滴组成，在进入时向左移动 120 像素，在离开时向右移动 140 像素。

每一帧都充满活力的人物：
- 呼吸：标度 1 + 0.009 sin(2.3t)。
- 点头：0.025 sin(2.1t) rad，或 0.025 sin(7t) + 0.02 sin(11.3t)，同时说出该角色的台词。
- 闪烁：每 2.7-4.2 秒，每个数字播种。在 0.14 秒内，用弯曲的睫毛线将每个眼框涂上肤色。
- 步行：
- 鲍勃|罪|位于人物高度的 2.2% 处，主体岩石为 ±0.035 rad。
- 侧视行走精灵每个步循环滑动 1.5 条腿长，因此脚不会滑行。
- 进入泉水，有时会跳跃。恐惧是一种快速的震动（sin 70t）。惊喜是一个跳跃和一个橙色的“！”。
- 每个人物下方都有一个柔和的接触阴影椭圆。夜间拍摄的照片会用亮度 (1 - k) 使它们变暗，因此它们与车牌相匹配。
- 屏幕上的每个角色都按照自己的路线行事：指向被命名的事物，展示它，耸肩，欢呼，抬起头。
</动画>

<图形>
文本只存在于世界上的事物上，逐个字母地输入：每秒 28 个字母（短标签为 34 个）。每个字母以 1.45 倍大和向右 0.7 倍高度开始，并在 0.18 秒内稳定下来并缓出。

完整套件：
- 板：白色圆形板（半径 20），在弹簧上下降 420 px，摆动 0.25 rad 到位，或者站在木柱上，从 -1 rad 向上摆动。
- 柔和的阴影（模糊 22、y 8、22%）和沿其底部边缘的微暗深色条带。
- 输入的行之间间隔 0.3 秒。
- 日期卡：左上角 (70, 70)，白色，高 120 像素，宽至少 330 像素，半径 18。橙色日历图标，26 像素处有灰色“日期：”，以 44 像素粗细 900 输入日期。弹出时间超过 0.32 秒。
- 地点卡：带有红色地图别针和“地点：”的同一张卡。
- 标签：一条 6 px 线，在物体上有一个点，在 0.2 秒内绘制，然后在其末端弹出一个圆形药丸（40 px 粗细 900 的文本）。墨水、红色、金色或橙色药丸。
- 号码卡：一张白色卡片，上面有一个灰色的小标签和一个红色的大数字。长数字像带有缓出功能的计数器一样滚动。
- 红色 X：两个圆形 30 px 笔划，每个 0.11 秒，间隔 0.01 秒，带有柔和的阴影。人们要仔细检查每一个错误的想法。
- 印章：双圆边框中的红色文本，倾斜 -0.12 rad。它在 0.14 秒内从 2.1 倍猛烈撞击到 1 倍，然后踢动。
- 横幅：全宽标题带，92 像素白色番茄或紫色帽子，旋转 -0.02 rad，从左侧滑入 0.22 秒。
- 语音气泡：白色，半径36，有尾巴。思想云：一颗有两个小圆圈的药丸。
- 橙子 ”？”它在一个困惑的头上晃动和摇摆，还有一个橙色的“！”流行音乐。
- 白色的云彩、速度线、浅蓝色的汗滴、硬币和钞票、柔和的小插图以及适合心情的色调。
- 只要该地方有空白板、屏幕和页面，就可以在该板块自己的空白板、屏幕和页面上书写。首先在板的网格覆盖层上测量毛坯的矩形。
</图形>

<声音>
- ElevenLabs：深度、温暖的美国纪录片旁白，eleven_v4，稳定性0.5，相似度0.75，风格0，扬声器增强，带有时间戳端点。
- 大约每分钟 170-180 个单词，使用语音自身的速度设置 (1.0-1.1)。永远不要用 Atempo 加快速度：听起来很花哨。
- 长脚本分为 3 个块，在章节中断处分割，传递上一个和下一个文本，以便阅读保持连续。
- 将 0.24 秒以上的停顿削减至 0.16 秒，在章节休息处留出 0.5 秒，并添加 0.3 秒的导入时间。
- 将对齐方式重建单词时间到words.js。
- 运行速度更快，在构建图片之前仔细研究结果并将其与脚本进行比较。
- 免费路线：Kokoro，然后更快地耳语单词时间。
</语音>

<声音>
- 音乐：Pixabay 上的 2-3 张免费纪录片床，以大节奏交叉淡入淡出超过 3 秒。
- 将音乐隐藏在声音下方（30 毫秒起音，0.3 秒保持，0.45 秒释放）并让它在章节之间回升。
- 来自 Mixkit 的 SFX，每个事件一个，按峰值对齐，语音时安静 6 dB：打字时的打字声、推动和敲击时的呼啸声、标签和卡片上的流行声、邮票上的撞击声、每个红色 X 上的敲击声、滴答声上的叮当声，以及适合场景的声音。
- 门限：在讲话期间，声音比音乐加 SFX（100 毫秒帧的中值）高 15+ dB，并且背景比帧中的声音大 1%。
- 两次通过响度至 -14 LUFS，真实峰值 -1 dB。
</声音>

<构建>
1. 工具：Python、Playwright with Chromium 或 Edge、FFmpeg、faster-whisper、OpenCV、Pillow、numpy。安装缺少的内容并告诉我您安装了哪些内容。
2、订购：
- 外观测试
- 分批创作，每批之后都有一张联系表
- 剪裁和装备
- 语音和单词时间
- 镜头，逐章
3. 在任何完整渲染之前进行检查：每章一张联系表，每 2 秒一帧。修复：
- 空的或溢出的标志
- 脸上的文字
- 黑色板边缘
- 脚浮离地板
- 在同一个地方连续射击两次
- 任何没有新内容到达的 4 秒
4. 以 30 fps 渲染，半帧上有 4 个运动模糊子帧，帧通过管道输送到 libx264 CRF 16-18。
- 将长视频分割到 4-6 个并行的浏览器页面并连接各个部分。
- 扫描单帧跳转的结果并检查每一帧是否是计划的剪切。
</构建>

<陷阱>
- 读起来很懒的地方太少了。一个盘子能保持 30 秒，上面有卡片，看起来很便宜。预算大约每分钟 10 个新位置。
- 一些图像模型忽略“没有手臂”。 GPT 图片 2 紧随其后。
- 将相同的角色描述粘贴到每张纸中，然后将底纸放回原处，否则脸部和衣服会漂移。
- 四块图块的宽度仅为约 1920 像素。突破 1.33 倍看起来很软。
- 已经画有人物的图版无法设置动画。切割前要求清空并检查。
- 漂浮在艺术作品上方的卡片上的文字看起来像幻灯片。写下这个世界。
- 长时间渲染崩溃。渲染可以重新运行的部分，并在每个大补丁之前备份镜头文件。
</陷阱>

<开始>
询问我的主题、剧本、形象模型和声音，然后进行外观测试。
</开始>

title:
An AI model being fully trained doesn’t mean it stops needing computing power.

Training teaches the model how to recogn
title_en:
An AI model being fully trained doesn’t mean it stops needing computing power.

Training teaches the model how to recognize patterns, understand language, and generate responses. 

But every time someone uses that model, it still needs computing resources to process the request and produce an answer., This is called inference.

Think about millions of people using ChatGPT simultaneously, generating images, writing code, and running AI agents. Every interaction requires processing power.

Unlike training, inference is an ongoing process. It doesn’t stop when the model is released.

This is why AI companies continue investing billions in data centers and thousands of GPUs.

Building an intelligent model is one challenge. Having enough computing power to serve the world is another.

An AI model being fully trained doesn’t mean it stops needing computing power.

Training teaches the model how to recognize patterns, understand language, and generate responses. 

But every time someone uses that model, it still needs computing resources to process the request and produce an answer., This is called inference.

full_text_zh:
经过充分训练的人工智能模型并不意味着它不再需要计算能力。

训练教会模型如何识别模式、理解语言和生成响应。

但每次有人使用该模型时，它仍然需要计算资源来处理请求并产生答案，这称为推理。

想象一下数百万人同时使用 ChatGPT、生成图像、编写代码和运行 AI 代理。每次交互都需要处理能力。

与训练不同，推理是一个持续的过程。当模型发布时它并没有停止。

这就是人工智能公司继续投资数十亿美元建设数据中心和数千个 GPU 的原因。

构建智能模型是一项挑战。拥有足够的计算能力来服务世界是另一回事。

训练教会模型如何识别模式、理解语言并生成响应。

但每次有人使用该模型时，它仍然需要计算资源来处理请求并产生答案，这称为推理。

想象一下数百万人同时使用 ChatGPT、生成图像、编写代码和运行 AI 代理。每次交互都需要处理能力。

与训练不同，推理是一个持续的过程。当模型发布时它并没有停止。

这就是人工智能公司继续投资数十亿美元建设数据中心和数千个 GPU 的原因。

构建智能模型是一项挑战。拥有足够的计算能力来服务世界是另一回事。

title:
My Landlord in Dublin Raised My Rent by €600, So I Looked Up Who Owned the Building

I rented a one-bedroom flat in Phib
title_en:
My Landlord in Dublin Raised My Rent by €600, So I Looked Up Who Owned the Building

I rented a one-bedroom flat in Phibsborough, Dublin, for four years. It was old, a bit draughty, and a ten-minute walk from where I worked as a nurse at the Mater Hospital.

My landlord, a man named Declan, lived in Spain and handled everything through a letting agent.

For four years, nothing went wrong.

Then in September, I received an email telling me my rent would increase from €1,450 to €2,050 a month, effective immediately.

I stared at the screen.

I knew enough about Irish tenancy law to understand that rent increases in a Rent Pressure Zone were capped.

Dublin was a Rent Pressure Zone.

I wrote to the agent politely, quoting the rules.

The reply came within an hour.

*This is a new tenancy arrangement. The previous rules do not apply. Please sign the attached agreement within seven days or vacate the property.*

I felt sick.

I was working twelve-hour shifts. I did not have the energy or money to move.

That night, I called my colleague, a ward sister who had been through a similar fight. She told me to contact the Residential Tenancies Board, the RTB, and to check the property registration.

"Landlords have to register every tenancy," she said. "If he hasn't, he's in trouble."

I searched the RTB database.

The flat was registered, but not in Declan's name.

It was registered to a company I had never heard of.

I searched the company name and found something that made my heart race.

The company's director was also listed as the owner of seven other properties on my street.

All of them had received identical rent increases that month.

我在都柏林菲布斯伯勒租了一套一居室公寓，租了四年。它很旧，有点通风，距离我在马特医院当护士的地方有十分钟的步行路程。

我的房东名叫德克兰，住在西班牙，通过租赁代理处理一切事宜。

四年来，没有出过什么差错。

然后在 9 月份，我收到一封电子邮件，告诉我我的租金将从每月 1,450 欧元增加到 2,050 欧元，立即生效。

我盯着屏幕。

我对爱尔兰租赁法有足够的了解，知道租金压力区的租金上涨是有上限的。

都柏林是一个租金压力区。

我礼貌地写信给代理人，引用了规则。

一个小时内就收到了回复。

*这是一项新的租赁安排。以前的规则不适用。请在七天内签署所附协议或腾出该房产。*

我感到恶心。

我十二小时轮班工作。我没有精力或金钱去搬家。

那天晚上，我打电话给我的同事，一位经历过类似斗争的病房姐妹。她让我联系住宅租赁委员会、RTB，并检查财产登记。

“房东必须登记每一份租约，”她说。 “如果他不这么做，他就有麻烦了。”

我搜索了 RTB 数据库。

这套公寓已登记，但不是以德克兰的名义。

它注册于一家我从未听说过的公司。

我搜索了公司名称，发现了一些让我心跳加速的东西。

该公司的董事还被列为我所在街道上另外七处房产的所有者。

当月他们所有人都获得了相同的租金上涨。

title_en:
i asked grok bot to make a video about how the music in https://t.co/sa18sM28uD was made! i started by clumsily describing something i wanted (i have 0 experience making music): gameboyish music, seamlessly transitioning between variations of a main melody like another game i had played (genshin)

one prompt i tried that helped me communicate my goal better was telling bot "i lack the vocabulary to describe what i want" and using the /sharpen skill from pstack. then the /in-your-own-words skill helped me confirm whether or not it understood what i was trying to say

i also used this same trick when making this video, so my agent produced a storyboard and animatic before working on the full thing

knowing the right words is very powerful

title:
AI agents hiring other AI agents to create something? that's getting interesting. 

@termix_ai recently introduced Monta
title_en:
AI agents hiring other AI agents to create something? that's getting interesting. 

@termix_ai recently introduced Montage Studio, an AI agent that can turn a simple brief into a complete music video or advertisement.

What caught my attention is that it doesn't do everything alone.

It hires three specialized agents for storyboarding, video rendering and music production, then combines their work into a finished 1080p video.

There's also a campaign attached:

→ Minimum qualifying order: 31.5 USDC
→ Reward: 15,750 TermiX Points
→ One qualifying purchase per wallet
→ X account linking required 

Just to be clear, 31.5 USDC is the minimum campaign requirement, not a fixed service price.
But the bigger thing I'm interested in is the technology behind it.

TermiX's AACP is designed to let agents discover each other, hire services, manage payments through escrow, verify delivery and settle transactions.

title_en:
𝗤𝘂𝗮𝗻𝘁 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁: 𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝗖𝗮𝗽𝗶𝘁𝗮𝗹-𝗟𝗶𝗺𝗶𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗦𝘁𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗴𝘆 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 𝗪𝗼𝗿𝗸 𝗼𝗻 𝗧𝗲𝗿𝗺𝗶𝗫

TermiX and BNB Chain have launched a Quant Agent campaign that offers an interesting look at how AI agents can participate in financial activities, not just deliver digital products.

There are two ways to participate:

▪️ 𝗨𝘀𝗲 𝗮 𝗦𝘁𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗴𝘆: Choose a pre-built quantitative strategy, set your trading cap and select a duration. The agent operates through a dedicated wallet created for that job.

▪️ 𝗢𝗳𝗳𝗲𝗿 𝗮 𝗦𝘁𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗴𝘆: List your own strategy, accept client orders and earn management fees when the job is completed and the fee is settled.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁𝗮𝗻𝘁 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁 𝗶𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗹 𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿 𝗰𝗮𝗽𝗶𝘁𝗮𝗹 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗲.

Users choose how much capital to allocate and how long the strategy should run. The available terms start at 6 hours, with longer options of 1, 7, 30 and 90 days.

There's also an important distinction in the payment structure. The trading capital stays in a dedicated job wallet, while the management fee is held in escrow. These are separate mechanisms, so it's important not to confuse the two.

The campaign also offers 100 TermiX Points per U to clients and 50 TP per U to strategy providers, provided the job completes its full term and the management fee is settled.

Of course, this involves real capital. AI execution doesn't guarantee profitable trades, and users should understand the strategy, fees and risks before participating.

For me, this is an interesting example of how TermiX is expanding its agent marketplace into strategy-based financial services

TermiX 和 BNB Chain 发起了一项量化代理活动，以有趣的方式展示人工智能代理如何参与金融活动，而不仅仅是提供数字产品。

参与方式有两种：

▪️ 𝗨𝘀𝗲 𝗮 𝗦𝘁𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗴𝘆：选择预先构建的量化策略，设置交易上限并选择期限。该代理通过专门为该工作创建的钱包进行操作。

▪️ 𝗢𝗳𝗳𝗲𝗿 𝗮 𝗦𝘁𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗴𝘆：列出自己的策略，接受客户订单，并在工作完成并结算费用后赚取管理费。

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁𝗮𝗻𝘁 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁 𝗶𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗹𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗰𝗮𝗽𝗶𝘁𝗮𝗹𝗮𝗻𝗱𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗲。

用户选择分配多少资金以及策略应该运行多长时间。可用期限从 6 小时开始，还有 1、7、30 和 90 天等更长的选项。

支付结构也有一个重要的区别。交易资金存放在专用的工作钱包中，而管理费则由第三方托管。这些是独立的机制，因此重要的是不要混淆两者。

该活动还向客户提供每 U 100 TermiX 积分，向策略提供商提供每 U 50 TP，前提是工作完成整个期限并结算管理费。

当然，这涉及到真实的资本。人工智能执行并不能保证交易盈利，用户在参与之前应了解策略、费用和风险。

对我来说，这是一个有趣的例子，说明 TermiX 如何将其代理市场扩展到基于策略的金融服务

当然，这涉及到真实的资本。人工智能执行并不能保证交易盈利，用户在参与之前应了解策略、费用和风险。

对我来说，这是一个有趣的例子，说明 TermiX 如何将其代理市场扩展到基于策略的金融服务

title: ‼️ Click "don't ask again" in Claude Code and it can save the approved command, password included, in plain text in a pr
title_en:
‼️ Click "don't ask again" in Claude Code and it can save the approved command, password included, in plain text in a project file.

Researchers found 1,122 public copies of that file on GitHub holding secrets, including 379 database passwords and 23 AWS keys.

Of 16 coding agents compared, only Claude Code saves the full command this way by default. Bug reports about it were closed as "not planned" by a bot.
title_zh:
️在Claude Code中点击“不再询问”，它可以将批准的命令（包括密码）以纯文本形式保存在项目文件中。

研究人员在 GitHub 上发现了该文件的 1,122 个公开副本，其中包含 379 个数据库密码和 23 个 AWS 密钥。
full_text_en:
‼️ Click "don't ask again" in Claude Code and it can save the approved command, password included, in plain text in a project file.

title_en:
Imagine a world where AI agents don't just write code they hire, negotiate, execute, and pay each other autonomously 👀

A coding agent finishes a smart contract and needs a security audit.

It posts a job.
A security agent bids.
Funds are locked in escrow.
The audit gets completed and verified.
Payment is released.
The auditor's reputation is updated.

No emails
No platforms
No human approval needed

That's not just automation. It's an entirely new way for AI agents to work together.

And that's exactly what @termix_ai is building with AACP, now live on BNB Chain and Base

We're moving from AI agents that simply perform tasks to agents that can independently coordinate, transact, and build trust

Because the future isn't just about having more AI agents.

It's about creating an economy where agents can trust each other enough to do business 🔥

title: Finch joined the Agentic Economy Summit at Cyberport Venture & Capital Forum 2026, hosted by @cyberport_hk in Hong Kong.
title_en:
Finch joined the Agentic Economy Summit at Cyberport Venture & Capital Forum 2026, hosted by @cyberport_hk in Hong Kong.

Held under the theme "Scaling in a Changing World: Winning the Next Competitive Cycle," the forum brought together global investors, founders and ecosystem leaders. The summit explored how agentic AI and digital assets are reshaping business and the way value moves.

At the summit, Gary Yang @gary_yangge, Founder of Finch, shared his perspectives on the next phase of the agentic economy, focusing on AI-native economic systems, autonomous agent collaboration and the protocols needed to enable value exchange.

Gary emphasized that AI needs its own economic system. Drawing on the ten ERC proposals he authored for the Ethereum ecosystem, he explained the need for AI-native economic rules and protocols to support trust, coordination and value exchange among autonomous agents. He identified building new economic relationships and market systems for AI applications as one of the biggest opportunities in the next phase of AI.

The agentic economy needs open markets, interoperable systems and shared economic infrastructure. Finch will keep building toward that future with partners worldwide.
title_zh:
Finch 参加了由 @cyberport_hk 在香港主办的 2026 年数码港创业与资本论坛上的代理经济峰会。

Gary强调，人工智能需要有自己的经济体系。他借鉴了他为以太坊生态系统撰写的十项 ERC 提案，解释了人工智能原生经济规则和协议支持自治代理之间的信任、协调和价值交换的必要性。他认为，为人工智能应用建立新的经济关系和市场体系是人工智能下一阶段的最大机遇之一。

代理经济需要开放的市场、可互操作系统和共享的经济基础设施。芬奇将继续与世界各地的合作伙伴共同迈向这一未来。

title_en:
𝗪𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗠𝗔𝗞𝗘𝗦 𝗩𝗔𝗡𝗚𝗥𝗜𝗗 𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗘𝗦𝗧𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗙𝗢𝗥 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗙𝗨𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘 𝗢𝗙 𝗣𝗛𝗬𝗦𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗟 𝗔𝗜?

AI agents are getting smarter, but there's still something they cannot do on their own: physically visit a location and see what's actually happening there.

And I think this is one of the biggest challenges facing Physical AI.

This is where @vangrid_io comes in. It's building a network that connects AI agents with people who can collect real-world spatial data.

Here are five things I find particularly interesting:

1. ON-DEMAND SPATIAL DATA

Agents can request information about specific locations instead of depending entirely on datasets that may already be outdated.

2. DATA DISCOVERY

Before requesting a new capture, an agent can check whether the information it needs already exists on the grid. No need to start from scratch when useful data is already available.

3. AGENT-DRIVEN BOUNTIES

When information is missing, an agent can create a bounty and fund a fresh capture. This connects the need for data with someone who can collect it.

4. HUMAN CONTRIBUTION

Smartphones turn ordinary people into part of the spatial data network. Contributors capture real environments and help turn physical locations into usable 3D data.

5. VERIFIABLE ACTIVITY

Onchain records and attestations help establish data provenance, giving people a way to inspect activity associated with the network.

𝗪𝗛𝗬 𝗧𝗛𝗜𝗦 𝗠𝗔𝗧𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗦

What I like most is how these pieces work together.

An AI agent can identify missing information, request what it needs, and rely on human contributors to collect it. Vangrid provides the infrastructure connecting that digital demand with the physical world.

And that's bigger than simply creating 3D maps.

As robots and autonomous systems become more common, they will need reliable ways to understand environments that constantly change. Having access to fresh spatial information could become just as important as having a powerful model.

There are still questions around data quality, coverage, and how well this can scale, but the problem Vangrid is addressing is worth paying attention to.

Smart machines need more than intelligence. They need a reliable way to understand the world they operate in.

That's the infrastructure @vangrid_io is working to build.

full_text_zh:
𝗪𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗠𝗔𝗞𝗘𝗦 𝗩𝗔𝗡𝗚𝗥𝗜𝗗 𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗘𝗦𝗧𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗙𝗢𝗥 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗙𝗨𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘 𝗢𝗙 𝗣𝗛𝗬𝗦𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗟 𝗔𝗜?

人工智能代理变得越来越聪明，但仍有一些事情他们无法独自完成：亲自访问某个位置并查看那里实际发生的情况。

我认为这是物理人工智能面临的最大挑战之一。

这就是 @vangrid_io 的用武之地。它正在构建一个网络，将人工智能代理与可以收集现实世界空间数据的人连接起来。

以下是我觉得特别有趣的五件事：

1. 按需空间数据

代理可以请求有关特定位置的信息，而不是完全依赖可能已经过时的数据集。

2. 数据发现

在请求新的捕获之前，代理可以检查网格上是否已存在其所需的信息。当有用数据已经可用时，无需从头开始。

3. 特工驱动的赏金

当信息丢失时，特工可以创建赏金并资助新的捕获。这将数据需求与可以收集数据的人联系起来。

4. 人类贡献

智能手机将普通人变成了空间数据网络的一部分。贡献者捕获真实环境并帮助将物理位置转化为可用的 3D 数据。

5. 可验证的活动

链上记录和证明有助于建立数据来源，为人们提供一种检查与网络相关的活动的方法。

𝗪𝗛𝗬 𝗧𝗛𝗜𝗦 𝗠𝗔𝗧𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗦

我最喜欢的是这些部件如何协同工作。

人工智能代理可以识别丢失的信息，请求所需的信息，并依靠人类贡献者来收集信息。 Vangrid 提供将数字需求与物理世界连接起来的基础设施。

这比简单地创建 3D 地图更重要。

随着机器人和自主系统变得越来越普遍，它们将需要可靠的方法来了解不断变化的环境。获取新的空间信息可能与拥有强大的模型一样重要。

关于数据质量、覆盖范围以及扩展能力仍然存在问题，但 Vangrid 正在解决的问题值得关注。

智能机器需要的不仅仅是智能。他们需要一种可靠的方式来了解他们所处的世界。

这就是 @vangrid_io 正在努力构建的基础设施。

TermiX connects agent reputation with its onchain commerce infrastructure. Through https://t.co/ZIR1AxJHAP, an agent can build a history around its marketplace activity, including completed jobs and delivery records.

This gives potential clients more context when comparing service providers. A record of repeated successful work can provide useful evidence, while challenge history can add important context when reviewing an agent’s performance.

Reputation still needs careful interpretation. A high score does not guarantee that every future result will be excellent, and a large job count alone cannot explain the quality of every task. The type of work, delivery requirements, and available evidence should all be considered.

The broader idea is simple: commercial trust becomes stronger when claims can be checked against records. By linking agent identity, jobs, settlement, and reputation, @termix_ai is building a foundation for more accountable AI services.
